title: Offboard doesnt want to enable after a is_active() check.
author: mcelhennyi
body:
MavSDK version v0.35.1

I am having an issue where the offboard does not want to enable. It seems like a few things...a race condition with a bad check (mavsdk side) and a bad way of checking the state of offboard (my side).

I was checking if the _offboard->is_active() but that was always true (because _mode != Mode::NotActive - it was PositionNed) before calling _offboard->start()...this was not a good way of doing it because even when the is_active switched to false so I could start the offboard (which happened periodically randomly) it would respond back with a failure because 
```
        if (_mode == Mode::NotActive) {
            return Offboard::Result::NoSetpointSet;
```
(offboard_impl.cpp)^^


How I fixed it: 

In process_heartbeat() i changed `_mode != Mode::NotActive` to `_mode == Mode::NotActive` . This caused the race condition of the NotActive being set too quickly to not happen anymore...

AND 

I, instead of checking is_active(), I check that `_flightMode != Telemetry::FlightMode::Offboard` and this allowed it to go into the offboard mode and respect my movement commands. 

My code is [here.](https://github.com/mcelhennyi/NXP-HoverGames-2/blob/ebc11e9577710f4cf036a230838d943761f902f8/code/src/system/agent/Agent.cpp#L305) 

I am not sure if the changes I made are proper and dont want to PR them without a discussion about this issue first. 

I also have been conversing with @JonasVautherin [here](https://px4.slack.com/archives/C68J8H32A/p1612241663087100) about this issue if you would like some more context.

answer_comments.body:
> I think calling start makes sense, but I also think its valuable for start to return the success or failure of switching from whatever mode its in to Offboard mode. 

Yes, I think we should probably add that. So we try to start offboard mode and then we wait until it's actually active. Once it's active, we return.

And in the same way we could have `is_active` check both, if setpoints are sent *and* if the mode is offboard.

> Is this actually a problem that can happen? Or is the printf maybe incorrect?

Technically my wording is incorrect (TARGETING_MODE vs RETURN_TO_LAUNCH) - bad copy-pasta....but the set position does return a status, although I have not seen it result in anything other than success in my testing.

It should always return "Success" unless there is a connection problem in which case nothing will work anymore.
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/14c5154c42f926addb303b8d6b26a4b6b03a81f4/src/plugins/offboard/offboard_impl.cpp#L353-L354

So, let me try to rephrase the problem:
We have two states:
1. The PX4 flight mode which can be set to offboard or not.
2. The mode of the MAVSDK offboard class which is some setpoint, or `NotActive`.

The way `start()` works is that it requires some setpoint to be set beforehand. If that's the case it should switch the mode to offboard. So then my question is which was the failure case that you got into that meant that you needed to check `is_active()`?
Or what was the problem that you ran into in the first place?

I checked is_active() because it seemed like (before I looked into the code base) that this would be a good thing to check before commanding it to start() since I wouldnt want to start then start again (that felt like bad form). Then come to find out is_active() seems more useful internally as a way to see if a setpoint was set or not...but like I said above even internally there was a flaw with it being set back to NotActive too quickly. At some points it would allow me past the isActve with a false return and then I would command a start to only be told that it didnt have a set point set...which i had just set a few lines above. 

But yes, I think there are two states/requirements:
1) the state the drone is actually in (offboard/stabilize/etc) - which should drive a users decision to start or stop offboard.
2) The internal mode that allows for the offboard mavsdk system to bark at you for not setting set points recently enough. (isActive()) - which in the current state should really not even be used by the user.

> At some points it would allow me past the isActve with a false return and then I would command a start to only be told that it didnt have a set point set...which i had just set a few lines above.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2269a0cfa6e225ee89be600d38dcb83c78283acc/src/plugins/offboard/offboard_impl.cpp#L617-L622
Basically, the point is that you set a setpoint and then immediately start it. If it's not started within 1.5 seconds, it will timeout again. I see how that is a bit confusing.
We could think about removing this timeout, or making it longer.

Alternatively, we could think of changing the API so that the user never has to call `start()` at all. Instead as soon as you set the first setpoint it automatically starts sending that setpoint and then tries to switch the mode. Once the mode is in offboard it would confirm.

`offboard.autoStart = true`/`offboard.enableAutoStart()` maybe?

But yea, it would reset there. One of the changes I made, but was unsure of its correctness was changing the != to == for the _mode part of that if(). However I made that change then (i think) immediately made the telemetry mode change as well. So not sure what effect (if any) that != to == had.

I think calling start makes sense, but I also think its valuable for start to return the success or failure of switching from whatever mode its in to Offboard mode. That would make the most sense, since offboard being started means two things: 1) The set point is set and the thread that sends them to the AP is in fact running AND 2) the AP mode has changed to offboard succesfully and the system is using the set points as expected.

> I think calling start makes sense, but I also think its valuable for start to return the success or failure of switching from whatever mode its in to Offboard mode. 

Yes, I think we should probably add that. So we try to start offboard mode and then we wait until it's actually active. Once it's active, we return.

And in the same way we could have `is_active` check both, if setpoints are sent *and* if the mode is offboard.
I agree, that makes the most sense to me.

Regarding the bug:

I've looked a bit into the source code. I don't fully understand it, but in short:

`paramServer.provide_param_custom("OHD_UART_NAME","/dev/ttyUSB0");`

is not a mavlink parameter but a mavlink extended parameter:

But for some reason the receiver calls 
` MAVLinkParameters::ParamValue::get_4_float_bytes_bytewise()`

on the extended parameter (which obviously is a string, not a float or int).

` MAVLinkParameters::ParamValue::get_4_float_bytes_bytewise()`

why - cannot tell yet ;)

`get_all_params();`

since when I explicitly request it using the custom keyword:
`get_param_custom("OHD_UART_NAME");`

It works. So when writing the implementation in mavsdk, the author did not consider that on a call to
`get_all_params()`

the server might provide mixed mavlink params and mavlink custom params.
I am not sure if mixing params and custom params into one plugin was a good idea ;)

Another thing, when looking at the code:
`get_all_params()`
would fetch all parameters (extended and non-extended).
But the imlementation only uses:
`mavlink_msg_param_request_list_pack`
and misses
`mavlink_msg_param_ext_request_list_pack`

So in theory get_all_params() should completely ignore extended params anyways ?
Honestly not completely sure. I'd say if the `param` plugin can automatically handle param vs param_ext, then that's better.

any idea how to run the tests under src/system_tests ?
The above should also be easily reproducable by extending the tests there.

thank you, I guess we have to wait then :/ I think the issue here is not easily fixable, at least for me. The more I read the code, the more worried I get how abstract the mavlink_parameters class actually is (aka what exactly can you use it for - to _**exchange configuration settings between MAVLink components**_ (which would be mavlink specification) or to _**exchange non-extended parameters between ground controll and PX4 FC and extended parameters between ground controll and a camera component**_

Because I read comments like 
`// FIXME: extended currently always go to the camera component`
and
`MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT1); // FIXME: what should the component be?
`

which makes me worried if we can even use mavsdk "parameters" for our intended purpose
(exchange non-extended and extended parameters between mavlink components)

> which makes me worried if we can even use mavsdk "parameters" for our intended purpose
(exchange non-extended and extended parameters between mavlink components)

The functions to set params (e.g. `set_param_int`) take a component id and a boolean telling them if it should use the extended microservice or not:

```c++
MAVLinkParameters::Result SystemImpl::set_param_int(
    const std::string& name,
    int32_t value,
    std::optional<uint8_t> maybe_component_id,
    bool extended)
{
    return _params.set_param_int(name, value, maybe_component_id, extended);
}
```

So it is possible at the lower level. Maybe even from the MavlinkPassthrough plugin.

Now the question is the interface: should the param plugin allow you to set the component id, or should the component id be abstracted away by MAVSDK? My intuition would be that it should be abstracted away. For instance, the camera plugin uses the params under the hood, but exposed as camera settings.

So somehow the param plugin talks to the autopilot, and the param server maybe should represent an autopilot? Then the camera plugin talks to a camera, and the camera server uses params under the hood, but not directly the params server.

What do you think?

Yeah, so the `set_xxx` take extended as a param, but that alone doesn't really help. 

I am pretty sure I now understand how the issue arrises (not 100% sure):

1) The server gets a get_all request (non-extended)
-> it then needs to respond with all the parameters 
-> it does so by just taking all the parameters it stores and sending them out as PARAM_VALUE

But oops, since the server has a parameter which is std:.string of type and non-ext cannot handle strings it fails.

This exact issue can then be mitigated by just making sure the server ignores parameters that do not fit into non-ext messages.

And when I do that in code, at least the server doesn't crash anymore as described above.

But now we've made the param class even more complicated .

Which then brings us back to the original question weather one should mix non-ext and ext ;)

My Opinion is the following:

1) A mavlink parameter server (or provider) is defined easily:
a) Store settings
b) allow changing settings (parameters) when requested by another mavlink system
c) provide current state of parameters to other mavlink systems when requested
d) notify the program (itself) of changes in the stored settings 

Now in theory, it would be possible to implement the param server that it works both with non-ext and ext messages - but then one would have to make sure that internally stored parameters that only work on extended (aka strings) only make it out to requesting components that speak extended (and then need to speak extended exclusively).

Which makes an already really complex class like MAVLinkParameters even more complex ;). 
(and I fear that only fixing the bug as described above is not the only one).


R.n I don't really have a solution for all these issues/bugs - or at least not a solution that doesn't require like >20h of programming ;).

But on a side note, I noticed the complete lack of documentation in the code under src/core/mavlink_parameters.h.c . Is there an internal documentation that is not published or is there simply no documentation at all ?

2) With the fix I proposed before, the get_all_params() now doesn't work anymore if there are parameters that need the ext. protocoll - the class would have to track the count of parameters seperatively for ext and non-ext.
Oh nice! Could you open a PR with your fix for 1? That's already worth it, right?

Sure, I'd love to talk to the author though, these changes might have implications one cannot see immediately.

get_all_params() is now working again, but obviosly only returns parameters that do not neccessarily need the extended protocoll.

Ideally, we'l have 
get_all_params_non_extended() and
get_all_params_extended() soon.
Interesting, I will have a closer look next week.

In an effort to build capabilities while testing and learning mavsdk I have been modifying some of the example code in MavSDK Java to talk with a SITL Arducopter drone.

My Environment:
	- Windows 11 host
	- Ardupilot SITL using WSL Linux ubuntu
	- Mavsdk server from [Releases](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v2.0.0/mavsdk_server_musl_x86_64) hosted in Alpine 3.19 docker
	-  MavSDKJava examples running from intellij gradle task

The Issue:
When attempting to start a mission upload using the code snippet below I get a "TIMEOUT" return after just a second or 2. This error happens regardless of using MissionRaw or Mission plugins.

To Reproduce:
	- run mavsdk server  v2.0 using `./mavsdk_server --sysid 10 --compid 10 udp://:14450  -p 50051`

	- run the SITL using: `sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map --location MCTSSA --instance 0`
	- Manually give your drone a mission of fly-to points using the draw or edit features in MavProxy or otherwise get a mission to the drone

Yes, there is an offset between how PX4 and Ardupilot interprete the mission. It should be fixed for Ardupilot in the mission implementation. I think it should not be too much work, but... somebody using Ardupilot should look into it :innocent:.

Would you be willing to have a look?

> Would you be willing to have a look?

I am about to take a deeper dive into the c++ code for another implementation so I will see if I can try and figure out the issue then. 

I am new to this code base and rusty with C++ so it may take me a lot more time than someone else to figure out the issue lol.

If someone else who uses Ardupilot gets the time or inclination that would also be a great help
Also have a look at this, maybe: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2058

> I think it should not be too much work, but... somebody using Ardupilot should look into it 😇.

I don't think that will magically be fixed. That's been like this for 10 years and I don't think it's trivial to fix it an also make it backwards compatible.

> I don't think that will magically be fixed. That's been like this for 10 years and I don't think it's trivial to fix it an also make it backwards compatible.

I was not referring to fixing this in MAVLink (I actually think that it is *not* possible in a backward compatible way). I was more thinking about some `if (ardupilot) { ... } else { ... }` in the MAVSDK mission logic. Don't you think that should be feasible?
Ah, yes, that's what we should do.

@julianoes @JonasVautherin I appear to have found (or, more accurately, been lead to by a colleague) the specific issue I am having with mission upload.

It appears that this line https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_mission_transfer_client.cpp#L325
`if (_sender.autopilot() == Autopilot::ArduPilot) {`

is not true when running the server in my environment.

I have run tests changing the line to
`if(true) {`
for the sake of quick confirmation and the mission raw upload succeeds!

Why the autopilot is not set to APM I do not know yet but that is the cause... it is never running the APM version of mission upload.

I am a little swamped with using the mission upload to look in more detail now but I plan to run a test to see exactly what the `_sender.autopilot()` is at that time but I don't have the time for a rebuild at the moment.

> and the mission raw upload succeeds!

Oh you are using mission_raw? I always assumed it was mission, which has the indexing problem. The mission_raw plugin should work with Ardupilot, I am pretty sure that some people are using it already :+1:.

>  I plan to run a test to see exactly what the _sender.autopilot() is at that time but I don't have the time for a rebuild at the moment.

Let us know what you find!
Hm, so you're creating a "fake" autopilot but want it to behave like ArduPilot, is that right?

I don't think so - I'm just uploading waypoints to an ardupilot with mission_raw. It worked fine with MAVSDK 1.x until the refactoring which added this TODO comment and returns Autopilot::Px4 no matter what is coming back from the connected device.

But this todo is only relevant for components which are used for `_server` plugins. So, if you're just connecting to ArduPilot, you would not be using a server plugin.

Can you reproduce this with the latest version? And if so, what's the exact error?

Ok, I did not use the really last version - looks like you fixed it in 30d2693417fe2afdfe494ace3e0f5b8ee5331f03 some weeks ago. But have to try it out during the next week an will report back if it really fixes the issue but it looks promising.
I can confirm that 30d2693417fe2afdfe494ace3e0f5b8ee5331f03 fixes the timeout problem for me.

I think I have [the same issue](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Java/issues/166), and it seems that you made it go away! What did you do? Please help if you can @chehrlic, I would appreciate it a ton!

linked_issues.title: Fix up installation and example docs when 130 deb fix goes in

comments.body:
The problem seems to be that `/usr/local/lib` is not in the `$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, at least on my Fedora.

You can workaround the problem using
```
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/usr/local/lib"
```

I need to research how other libraries do this.

According to http://tldp.org/HOWTO/Program-Library-HOWTO/shared-libraries.html it is ok to install libraries into `/usr/local/lib` when you compile from source, so during development.

For Ubuntu, all that is required after `sudo make default install` is `sudo ldconfig` to update the linker cache.
Thanks very much. I'll add a note in the build instructions and a troubleshooting section in the examples section.
Thanks!

I got the same error on my Fedora28. Setting the environment variable LD_LIBRARY_PATH didn't solve the problem. 
Also running the ldconfig didn't solve. I found that ldconfig looks into "/etc/ld.so.conf". Checking there I saw that there was no reference to those share libraries.
In the "etc/ld.so.conf" there is simply an include of the files *.conf contained in "etc/ld.so.conf.d/".

I added a new file called "dronecode.conf" containing the path to the libraries in that folder. Then, after running the ldconfig, it worked. 

p.s. The reference about the ldconfig: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/12045563/cannot-load-shared-library-that-exists-in-usr-local-lib-fedora-x64.
@rt-2pm2 can you please post the whole output? I'm doing this all the time in Fedora, so I have the feeling you're missing something somewhere.

@julianoes Sure, I am happy to participate. 
To restore the system in the condition before my changes:
1) Remove the "dronecode.conf" file from the "etc/ld.so.conf.d" folder. In this way it won't be included by ldconfig.
2) Run the `ldconfig`

I check that the libraries are in "/usr/local/lib"
> $ ls /usr/local/lib

libdronecode_sdk_calibration.so  libdronecode_sdk.so

libdronecode_sdk_gimbal.so      
libdronecode_sdk_info.so        
libdronecode_sdk_logging.so      
libdronecode_sdk_mission.so     

Now I try to run one  of my example without using my approach:
The LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable in my fedora is void. Thus, I assign the environment variable with 
> $ LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/usr/local/lib"
I update the linker cache running `ldconfig`

Then, when I run the executable (fly_auto), I get this output:
> $ ./fly_auto udp://127.0.0.1:6000                                            
./fly_auto: error while loading shared libraries: libdronecode_sdk.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

I hope that I answered your request.

@rt-2pm2 ok please try with `export`:
```
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/usr/local/lib"
```
Exactly! Glad I could help!

title: Building MAIN breaks Euler Angle Values - ArduCopter (Returns NaN but works in v1.4.16)
author: OliverHeilmann
body:
Hello!

I have been following #2031 as I had the same issue with the `GUIDED mode`. I could not get a drone to take off without manually setting it to `GUIDED mode` first. Thankfully, this issue has been solved now, thanks dev team! 

I followed the suggestion of building `main` from source and that has worked nicely so thank you. Unfortunately however, my previously working eulerAngle telemetry gets are now broken/ only return NaN values.

As the title suggests, this issue is raised for ArduCopter (and Rover, Plane etc.) and *not* for PX4 (which I have tried `main` and it works fine).

This is the code I used:
```cpp
mavsdk::Telemetry::EulerAngle eulerAngle = telemetry->attitude_euler();
```
Using `main` I get the following results for euler angle params:
![Screenshot 2023-09-20 at 22 07 27](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/49697817/6e0744b4-0246-4c74-9e43-6165b9100c0e)

Using `v1.4.16`, I get the following results for euler angle params:
![Screenshot 2023-09-20 at 22 05 02](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/49697817/645fac70-3017-4c64-8ed8-8ff6c3902c0c)

I suspect there is some code change that needs to be modified back to the `v1.4.16` version?

Thanks for your help in advance!

answer_comments.body: But how does it work then? If there is no default, then the client should always set it anyway, in order to get consistent behavior, right?

Actually the problem with MAVSDK setting a rate is that it will conflict with other clients. Say QGC sets some rate and then you start MAVSDK, then MAVSDK won't know about QGC and will just overwrite it.

That's a tricky problem :thinking:.

> Perhaps this is a quirk for ArduPilot and the way Mavlink messages are interpreted, or perhaps this is a MavSDK issue?

Sounds like something that MAVSDK should handle properly :+1:.

> I think it is reasonable to have some logic where you get_rate

I am not sure if MAVLink provides any way of getting the rate, though :thinking:. Not sure if there is a solution to that (other than pushing the problem to the application developers, that they need to tune for their particular app, use-case and drone) :confused:.

comments.body: Possible. Can you check whether ArduPilot sends out https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#ATTITUDE or https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#ATTITUDE_QUATERNION and what the values are?

Thanks for the speedy response. A few things to add here... 1) Using `mavsdk::Telemetry::Quaternion quaternionAngle = telemetry->attitude_quaternion();` I printed the outputs and they also read `NaN` as illustrated in the picture below: It is worth noting that these results are from the ArduPilot SITL environment. 2) I did the same test with physical drone hardware and I discovered that none of the telemetry data (including Lat/ Lon etc.) were sending at all. After opening Mission Planner, connecting to the drone, closing it again and then running my code, the other telemetry started sending (excluding the Euler and Quaternion angles as before). This reminds me of another Issue I raised a while back #1967. But to be clear, connecting is fine now, it's just the telemetry values returning NaN.
With Ardupilot, do you need to somehow enable some telemetry with `set_rate` or something?

> perhaps this is something that could be incorporated into MavSDK?

Yeah I wonder. It surely would be nice if it was consistent between PX4 and Ardupilot when using MAVSDK... Maybe MAVSDK should just set default rates for everything? @julianoes what do you think?
I don't think it should. It depends on the link and what you're trying to do. Otherwise, you end up with way too much traffic on the link, depending on the link of course.
But how does it work then? If there is no default, then the client should always set it anyway, in order to get consistent behavior, right?

How about setting a rate if/ when that specific telemetry type is requested? e.g.

```cpp
mavsdk::Telemetry::EulerAngle euler = telemetry->attitude_euler();    // inside attitude_euler() method somewhere
```

Some check to see if a rate has already been set or something... You'd still have to choose a number of course but then the user can at least change it if they decide they want to. Would need to think about cases where user `set_rate` then calls `get_telemetry` to ensure rate isn't overwritten but that's doable right?

**EDIT:** Also, why was it working in `v1.4.16`? Do you remember what changes were made since then?

Actually the problem with MAVSDK setting a rate is that it will conflict with other clients. Say QGC sets some rate and then you start MAVSDK, then MAVSDK won't know about QGC and will just overwrite it.

That's a tricky problem :thinking:.

Ok follow up observation here. 

I've noticed that when I set `set_rate_attitude_euler(...)` but **NOT** `set_rate_attitude_quaternion(...)`, I don't receive any telemetry for Euler *or* Quat angles. When I do the reverse (Quat and not Euler), I receive both Euler *and* Quat angles.

Perhaps this is a quirk for ArduPilot and the way Mavlink messages are interpreted, or perhaps this is a MavSDK issue? Not sure so thought I'd post here.

In regards to your other comment @JonasVautherin, I think it is reasonable to have some logic where you `get_rate` to check if a non-zero value has already been set, if so, don't overwrite it... could this solve your QGC problem description? Though, what this doesn't solve is the case where MavSDK sets a rate *first* and then QGC overwrites it right?

In any case, It would be good to actually get some telemetry if you are polling for it, regardless of rates. I wouldn't have posted this issue if I saw values returning for instance.

> Actually the problem with MAVSDK setting a rate is that it will conflict with other clients. Say QGC sets some rate and then you start MAVSDK, then MAVSDK won't know about QGC and will just overwrite it.
> 
> That's a tricky problem 🤔.

> Perhaps this is a quirk for ArduPilot and the way Mavlink messages are interpreted, or perhaps this is a MavSDK issue?

Sounds like something that MAVSDK should handle properly :+1:.

> I think it is reasonable to have some logic where you get_rate

I am not sure if MAVLink provides any way of getting the rate, though :thinking:. Not sure if there is a solution to that (other than pushing the problem to the application developers, that they need to tune for their particular app, use-case and drone) :confused:.

> I am not sure if MAVLink provides any way of getting the rate, though 🤔. Not sure if there is a solution to that (other than pushing the problem to the application developers, that they need to tune for their particular app, use-case and drone) 😕.

I see [MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL) and [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE) in the docs but, you're right, I don't see any way of getting current rate anywhere... interesting.

I am still wondering if it is clear to devs using MAVSDK with ArduPilot that they need to use `set_rate` to get the telemetry stream though?

Also wanted to raise a [seg-fault issue](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2031#issuecomment-1732363494) here too as I also encountered it when I changed my MAVSDK version to main and built from source (which is when I also discovered the Euler telemetry issue discussed above as well). I suggested re-opening the issue but can create a new one if you think it is sensible to do so.
The NaN euler values were fixed in PR #2212, which now uses directly-parsed ATTITUDE message values instead of quaternion conversion. Can this be closed?
Great, thanks or checking @PavelGuzenfeld.

title: MissionRaw stopped working from v1.2.0 to v1.3.0
author: prokas-nikos
body:
In my android app after uploading from io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.2.1 to io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.3.1 I noticed that I could not upload the mission. After downgrading to 1.2.1 the functionality was the same as before.

I could upload with 
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk:1.2.0'
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.2.1'

and could not upload with 
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk:1.3.0'
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.3.1'

In the log I am receiving a warning "W  Invalid sequence for ArduPilot items"  and in Wireshark I can not see any mavlink messages sent. The MISSION_COUNT message is not sent.
resolution_evidence: maintainer declares completion: 'This has been fixed'

answer_comments.body: I might be wrong on this and I should make a simple Python example to show it. It's clearly a bit of challenge.

> I am not sure about the status in v1.3.0, but i believe that release was from much before the addition of ardupilot mission validation check.

I backported it: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2065

It's part of [v1.4.15](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v1.4.15)

I need to update the Python wrappers to be based on top of it.
@JonasVautherin can you update the Java wrappers as well? Thanks.

This has been fixed in MAVSDK [v1.4.15](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v1.4.15), MAVSDK-Python [v1.4.7](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/releases/tag/1.4.7), and MAVSDK-Java [1.3.2](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Java/releases/tag/1.3.2).

Thanks @ykhedar and @JonasVautherin.

Hi @prokas-nikos,
The current sequence for mission sequence is 0,1,2,3, etc. We had incorrectly implemented ardupilot mission validation which has been now corrected and pushed to the main branch. I am not sure about the status in v1.3.0, but i believe that release was from much before the addition of ardupilot mission validation check. 

If you are using ArduPilot, I would suggest to use the main branch instead of specific tagged versions since many ardupilot related changes are in the main branch. After the release of v2.0 these should be available also in the release.

More information on how to setup and work with ArduPilot and MAVSDK are in this repository https://github.com/ykhedar/ardupilot-mavsdk which I specifically created to help devs like you get started with this combination. Give it a try and let me know if you face any problem.

@TheNishantK oh I have an idea. You're already using MAVROS in this case right? The problem is that DroneCore uses the same UDP port that MAVROS connects to. You could switch the DroneCore port to that one of QGroundControl if you don't need that one (14550). Otherwise, I don't recommend using DroneCore and MAVROS at the same time.

@TheNishantK I don't think you understood https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/364#issuecomment-382369537. 
QGroundControl binds to port 14550. So you can't bind to the same port in DroneCore while QGroundControl is running.
MAVROS binds to port 14540. So you can't bind to the same port in DroneCore while MAVROS is running.

What you can do:
- Close QGroundControl and launch DroneCore app using 14550.
- And then, launch MAVROS (which binds to 14540).

You could for instance keep 14550 untouched for QGC, and forward 14540 to, say, 14541 and 14542 for MAVROS and MAVSDK:

```sh

```

title: std::optional for CommandLong always returns true. Causes fault on Ardupilot
author: PeterQFR
body:
[Line 429](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_command_sender.cpp#L440) of mavlink_commands.cpp,  is a check to see if particular parameter on the command long has been set using the contextural conversion of std::optional. If it has not been set, the the value is initialised to certain values depending on whether the auto pilot is ardupilot or not. 

It does appear that this check always returns true, regardless if the param has been set. This maybe due to the initialisation of the values in CommandLong to NAN. This will result in ardupilot autopilots throwing a SIGFPE and closing the connection. This may be the cause of some of the problems in #728 and elsewhere particularly when SITL is used. 

I'm not sure of the correct solution but perhaps not initialising those parameters is probably an option?

answer_comments.body:
Oh, I think this one is wrong actually:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L515

It should be ~zero initialized~ default constructed.

Interesting, so for passthrough it's different... Well, given it's "raw passthrough" it's just up to the user. I would say it's best if you zero-initialize the struct before setting the rest of the values. Does that make sense?

I finally had a closer look at this. I can see where you're coming from. However, given it's a passthrough API, I would say that it's just up to the user to set all values to something that the flight stack can cope with. So, for PX4 that means filling the reserved values with NAN, and for ArduPilot it might have to be 0 in some (older AP versions?) cases as NAN will cause a fault. I'm reluctant to make this more complex than it is, unless you have a suggestion how this could easily be improved?

Closing, re-open if you still think this needs to be addressed and change.

comments.body: Aha, thanks for the note. Is this for all commands that are sent or just one specific one?

The Ardupilot failure comes from CommandLong. They try to convert it to a CommandInt for logging purposes and it is this that causes the fault. I comment out the conversion and I don't have problems. I also don't have commands logged though. 

Some of the values I have seen, particularly for param6 were uninitialised values e.g. 2.452.. e+38. In my code, I'm not initialising those values in the mavsdk::MavlinkPassthrough::CommandLong that I am using. 
This also faults during the systemImpl [sending of a command long](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L512) for autopilot capabilities.

I would have expected the check on Line429 to initialise those values to the correct ones, but it doesn't appear to work.
 The Values for command types are not std::optional in the MavlinkPassthrough[ definitions](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/include/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_passthrough.h#L87) of CommandLong or CommandInt. In this case as params are not initialised as a std::optional its probably part of the reason the check in mavlink_commands.cpp fails.

Actually, maybe this is only an issue with the mavlink passthrough command long. I went back undid my changes to ardupilot and initialised those parameters. I haven't seen it fault on the std::optional CommandLong used in systemImpl, I think I got that wrong. 
So I'd say this is limited to mavlink_passthrough CommandLong, as they are not initialised as std::optional. This makes more sense.

Oh, I think this one is wrong actually:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/system_impl.cpp#L515

It should be ~zero initialized~ default constructed.

what about the[ initialiser](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/include/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_passthrough.h#L87) for mavlink_passthrough::Command

Interesting, so for passthrough it's different... Well, given it's "raw passthrough" it's just up to the user. I would say it's best if you zero-initialize the struct before setting the rest of the values. Does that make sense?

Well they're not raw types to start with, ie. we are not interfacing with mavlink passthrough using mavlink_msg_command_long_t.
Its a new type defined in mavlink_passthrough, so I don't think the "raw passthrough" applies. It also, as far as I can tell, goes through the same code path and calls maybe_reserved() on its way out. I think a solution would be to typedef the mavlink_passthrough::CommandLong  definition to the one in [Mavlink Command Sender ](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/4dcee2b14945a80276f1b30abd99088ed7009d9f/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_command_sender.h#L57).

Its up to you, but it would solve this issue for future, assuming that the command in mavlink passthrough uses the code path through the mavlink command sender.
If it doesn't use the same code path, then it is probably not worth worrying about.
You're right, let me have a closer look later.

I finally had a closer look at this. I can see where you're coming from. However, given it's a passthrough API, I would say that it's just up to the user to set all values to something that the flight stack can cope with. So, for PX4 that means filling the reserved values with NAN, and for ArduPilot it might have to be 0 in some (older AP versions?) cases as NAN will cause a fault. I'm reluctant to make this more complex than it is, unless you have a suggestion how this could easily be improved?

Closing, re-open if you still think this needs to be addressed and change.

title: MAVSDK remote control hangs
author: MIKE9708
body:
Hi, i was trying to to use the MAVSDK python library to communicate with a drone in a  simulation ( the simulation is based on the PX4 repository using gazebo has a simulation tool ) hosted on a different machine. When i run the simulation and try :

``
drone = System()
await drone.connect(system_address="udp://ip_addr_of_target_machine:14540")
``

the script remains hanged, while on the simulation logs im able to see:

`INFO [mavlink] partner IP: ip_addr_of_MAVSDK_machine
`

Now looking on the [PX4 documentation](https://docs.px4.io/v1.12/en/simulation/) i read that there are a series of option in order to achieve what i want to do , i tried  **Enable UDP Broadcasting** , **Enable Streaming to Specific Address**,and   **Use MAVLink Router**, without being able to get any result.

Can anyone help me understand  if i am doing something wrong or the PX4 docu solution should be modified?
Thanks
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body: Seems like it should work with `udp://:14550` on the MAVSDK machine... :thinking:
Seems like it. Does QGC receive MAVLink if you run it instead of MAVSDK on your MAVSDK machine?
No, just launch QGC and verify that it can talk to the drone. If QGC doesn't work either, then it means that there is something wrong with your network setup.

comments.body:
You have it backwards. You can't connect to UDP 14540 being published on another computer.

What you can do is:
```python
drone = System()
await drone.connect(system_address="udp://:14540")
```

And now enable broadcast, or specifically set the IP in PX4 `mavlink start ... -t IP`.
Actually the UDP port that i am using is 14550 on the mavsdk side i followed [this](https://docs.px4.io/v1.12/en/simulation/#use-mavlink-routerl)

And does this work then?

```python
drone = System()
await drone.connect(system_address="udp://:14550")
```
Yes in localhost it works
And your problem is when the simulator is running on another machine? Do you have mavlink-router running on that other machine and sending MAVLink to the machine that is running MAVSDK?
yeah i got mavlink router running on the machine with the STL and from the other machine i am using mavsdk for comunicating
I've also read [this issue](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2149), where the guy was using the port 18570 on mavsdk side
Can you show your mavlink-router configuration file?

This my config file:

```

[UdpEndpoint QGC]
Mode = Normal
Address = 192.168.124.1 # MAVSDK machine
Port = 14550

[UdpEndpoint SIM]
Mode = Eavesdropping
Address = 127.0.0.1 # SITL
Port = 14550

```
Seems like it should work with `udp://:14550` on the MAVSDK machine... :thinking:
Wait you mean that on the mavsdk machine i should use the localhost for connecting?
Seems like it. Does QGC receive MAVLink if you run it instead of MAVSDK on your MAVSDK machine?
You mean launching QgroundControl with mavlink forwarding enable where i specify the IP addres of the MAVSDK machine?
No, just launch QGC and verify that it can talk to the drone. If QGC doesn't work either, then it means that there is something wrong with your network setup.
Ok but QGControl on the SITL machine or the mavsdk machine ? because if i launch it on the SITL machine it is able to detect the drone
And on the MAVSDK machine?
Yes Qgroundcontrol works and is able to detect the other machine
Ok i tried with another machine and it seems to work fine, i don't really know what was the problem, thanks for the time that you've dedicated me anyway

title: MavlinkDirect does not receive some messages via serial
author: matt-at-spsa
body:
I think I have found a bug in MavlinkDirect. The following MAVLink messages are (almost never) received when sent via a serial port, and subscribed to by MavlinkDirect:

```
HEARTBEAT 
SYS_STATUS
POWER_STATUS
MEMINFO
NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT
MISSION_CURRENT
GPS_RAW_INT
```
There may be others, but these are the missing messages I've found so far in my testing.

Tested with MAVSDK version 3.15, installed from `libmavsdk-dev_3.15.0_debian12_arm64.deb`

### Test Code

I have two different C++ scripts/files that I am using for this testing:

* [mavlink_message_listener.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26691963/mavlink_message_listener.cpp) - uses `mavsdk.intercept_incoming_messages_async` to print out **every** MAVLink message on the device. This seems to work accurately as far as I can verify with QGroundControl/MissionPlanner. So I do trust this script, and it is actually heavily based on one of the mavsdk examples IIRC.
* [mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26691988/mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp) - Iterates through a hard-coded list of MAVLink messages from both `serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:115200` and `udpin://192.168.1.6:14550` using BOTH **MavlinkDirect** and **MavlinkPassthrough**, then compiles a table of the results, populating it based on whether each message was received from that source. Full disclosure, this is a ChatGPT-generated script that is based off more basic scripts manually written by me, where I looked at each message one at a time. The result from this script matches what I have seen with my own, non-AI-generated scripts. I just wrote this script for convenience and to help you replicate my findings quickly.

### Expected Result:

I expect to see that every message is received (i.e. the message callback is called) for each message tested, regardless of whether it was subscribed to by MavlinkDirect OR MavlinkPassthrough, and regardless of the port used.

I have used mavlink_message_listener.cpp to verify that each message IS being sent to each UDP/serial port. 

### Actual Result:
This is the last part of the terminal output from mavsdk_message_matrix.cpp. It shows that there are seven message types that are NOT received by MavlinkDirect, but only when sent via serial. 

```
============================================================
Summary
============================================================

Message               | Direct  | Pass    | Direct  | Pass    |
----------------------| --------| --------| --------| --------|
                      | Serial  |         | UDP     |         |
----------------------| --------| --------| --------| --------|
GLOBAL_POSITION_INT   | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
LOCAL_POSITION_NED    | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
HEARTBEAT             | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW      | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
RC_CHANNELS           | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
COMMAND_ACK           | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
AUTOPILOT_VERSION     | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
SYS_STATUS            | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
POWER_STATUS          | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
MEMINFO               | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
NAV_CONTROLLER_OUTPUT | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
MISSION_CURRENT       | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
GPS_RAW_INT           | NO      | YES     | YES     | YES     |
TIMESYNC              | YES     | YES     | YES     | YES     |
```
Just to reiterate, these missing messages ARE being sent to the serial port, as shown by this mavlink_message_listener.cpp output:
```
spsa:~/test_code/build$ ./Release/bin/MavlinkMessageListener serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:115200
[INFO] Setting up MAVLink listener...
[11:30:22|Info ] MAVSDK version: v3.15.0 (mavsdk_impl.cpp:33)
Connecting to serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:115200
[11:30:22|Debug] Component Autopilot (component ID: 1) added. (system_impl.cpp:496)
[11:30:22|Debug] Discovered 1 component (system_impl.cpp:616)
Connected to Generic running Unknown
[INFO] Listener running. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
SEQ: 191 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    33 | GLOBAL_POSITION_INT
SEQ: 192 SYS:   1 COMP:   1 MSGID:    32 | LOCAL_POSITION_NED

answer_comments.body:
## Root Cause

After tracing through the code, the bug is in `LibmavReceiver` (the parser that feeds MavlinkDirect): it **only handles MAVLink v2** (`0xFD` magic byte). MAVLink v1 messages (`0xFE`) are silently skipped.

### How MavlinkDirect receives messages

When data arrives on a serial connection, MAVSDK runs two independent parsers on the same raw byte stream ([`serial_connection.cpp`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp#L322-L335)):

1. **Standard C library parser** (`MavlinkReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkPassthrough, `intercept_incoming_messages_async`, plugins, etc. Handles both MAVLink v1 and v2.
2. **libmav `BufferParser`** (`LibmavReceiver`) — feeds MavlinkDirect. **Only handles MAVLink v2.**

In [`BufferParser::parseMessage`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/core/serial_connection.cpp), the scan literally is:

```cpp
while (start_pos < buffer_size && buffer[start_pos] != 0xFD) {
    start_pos++;  // skips 0xFE (MAVLink v1 start byte) without parsing it
}
```

Any v1 message bytes are consumed/skipped, and `nullopt` is returned — so MavlinkDirect never sees them.

### Why it works over UDP but not serial

When connecting via UDP through a GCS relay (QGC / Mission Planner), the GCS has typically negotiated MAVLink v2 with the autopilot, so all forwarded messages arrive as v2. Over a direct serial connection, ArduPilot sends many common messages as MAVLink v1 by default (HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, GPS_RAW_INT, etc.). Those are exactly the ones missing.

The "sometimes works after power-on" behaviour is also consistent: if MAVSDK starts sending v2 heartbeats quickly enough, ArduPilot may switch those streams to v2 before the subscription is set up, making them visible for that session. After a power cycle, ArduPilot boots into v1 again.

The dialect question (MEMINFO in ardupilotmega.xml) is a red herring — the ardupilotmega XML *is* loaded, but that doesn't matter because the message is sent as v1 and the BufferParser never reaches the definition lookup.

### Fix

The cleanest fix is to bridge messages parsed by the standard C library into the libmav handler chain. Since the C library already handles v1+v2, every successfully parsed `mavlink_message_t` can be converted to a `Mavsdk::MavlinkMessage` (via the libmav MessageSet for field names and JSON serialization) and dispatched to `receive_libmav_message`. The independent libmav raw-stream parser could then be kept as a fallback only for custom messages loaded via `MavlinkDirect::load_custom_xml` that the C library doesn't know.

Alternatively, `BufferParser` could be extended to support MAVLink v1 (`0xFE`), but that requires converting the v1 wire format, and the C library approach is simpler and avoids duplication.

title: mavsdk_server crashes when a geofence is uploaded
author: JonasVautherin
body:
`mavsdk_server` gets a segmentation fault when uploading a geofence over gRPC.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Build `mavsdk_server` from #870.
2. Checkout MAVSDK-Python into the [python geofence PR](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/pull/114)
3. Run jmavsim and the `mavsdk_server` built in 1 above.
4. Run `examples/geofence.py` in MAVSDK-Python fetched in 2 above.
5. The geofence is uploaded successfully, but `mavsdk_server` crashes.

@coderkalyan: Would you mind having a look at this? :blush:.

answer_comments.body:
@coderkalyan I've been debugging that, and my observation is that the callback given to `send_geofence_async(...)` is called twice: once with result `Success`, and another time with result `Timeout` (which doesn't make sense to me if it succeeded before).

`mavsdk_server` crashes on the second call (with `Timeout`), because it expects the callback to be called exactly once.

Would you mind investigating why the timeout is called after a `Success` result is sent?

More specifically, the mission plugin unregisters the timeout on [`receive_command_result`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L1299-L1300), and maybe this mechanism is missing in the geofence plugin :thinking:.

It could be that it is something stupid in the geofence plugin with all the callbacks and locks happening there. I'm planning to refactor the mission and geofence plugin to clean these up, hopefully next week.
@coderkalyan good question. I would have to look into it and try it out.

title: Discrepancy between Documentation and Example
author: RizzwareEngineer
body:
I have the following basic `CMakeLists.txt` for my C++ code that makes use of the Telemetry API.

<details>
  <summary>CMakeLists.txt</summary>

```cpp

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.15)
project(telemetry-stream)

# Set the C++ standard
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# Enable strict handling of warnings
add_definitions("-Wall -Wextra -Werror")

# Find MAVSDK package
find_package(MAVSDK REQUIRED)

# Add executable target with source files
add_executable(telemetry-stream main.cpp)

# Link MAVSDK library
target_link_libraries(telemetry-stream
  MAVSDK::mavsdk
)
```

</details>

<details>
  <summary>Output</summary>

```
-- Configuring done (0.1s) CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:18 (target_link_libraries): Target "telemetry-stream" links to:
MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry
but the target was not found. Possible reasons include:

* There is a typo in the target name.
* A find_package call is missing for an IMPORTED target.
* An ALIAS target is missing.

According to [this documentation](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/telemetry.html), `MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry` is needed within the `target_link_libraries` call.

However, this [following example's](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/examples/takeoff_and_land.html) source code which makes use of Telemetry does **_NOT_** include `MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry` within the `target_link_libraries` call.

If I delete `MAVSDK::mavsdk_telemetry`, I am able to build and execute. 

However, I wanted to ask: why there is a discrepancy between the documentation and the example, and which I should follow?

resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
Ok. So part of what you did before was to install `python3.6` and `pip3.6`. On your system, you should now have multiple versions of Python. `python` is some Python 2 (maybe 2.7?), `python3` is Python 3.X (maybe 3.5?), and `python3.6` is Python 3.6 (the one you just installed).

The script `run_protoc.sh` calls `python3` and `pip3`, because on more modern systems like Ubuntu 18.04, that would be fine. But on your Ubuntu 16.04, you need the script to explicitly call `python3.6` and `pip3.6`.

So you should open `run_protoc.sh`, and replace `python3` with `python3.6` everywhere. And also replace `pip3` with `pip3.6` everywhere. Then save your changes and run `run_protoc.sh`.

If you're using Gazebo, you can try to run it without graphics:
```
HEADLESS=1 make px4_sitl gazebo
```

If you haven't installed Gazebo yet, and have Docker, you can also try to run it directly from [this docker image](https://github.com/JonasVautherin/px4-gazebo-headless) (have a look at the documentation there).

I see. I guess you may want to try Gazebo (see Julian's comment above).

I'm closing this issue now, as the Python wrapper got installed.

Below are the steps I followed for installing DronecodeSDK-Python on an Ubuntu 16.04 Docker container ([see the Dockerfile here](https://gist.github.com/JonasVautherin/0bdd08bf58a6f8022b7645b0a0415023)). Make sure to adapt those steps to your system if needed, and to read the output of those commands to make sure they don't fail.

1. Install prerequisites (in your case I believe you already have them):

```
$ apt install curl git software-properties-common
```

2. Clone the repository:
```
$ git clone https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python --recursive <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>
```

3. Install Python 3.6:

```
$ add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
$ apt update
$ apt install python3.6
```

Note that it won't replace `python` or `python3`, so `python3` will still point to `python3.5`. You can either change that (there are tutorials for this) or always call `python3.6` explicitly (which I do in these instructions).

4. I had to install pip3.6 manually:

```
$ curl https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | python3.6
```

5. Install `dcsdkgen`, needed to generate the Python SDK:

```
$ cd <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>/proto/pb_plugins

$ cd <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>
$ pip3.6 install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
$ sed -i 's/python3/python3.6/g' other/tools/run_protoc.sh
$ other/tools/run_protoc.sh
```

7. Finally, install the SDK:

```
$ cd <path/to/dronecodesdk_python>
$ pip3.6 install -e .
```

#!/bin/bash
SCRIPT_DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" && pwd )"
WORK_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../"
PROTO_DIR="${WORK_DIR}/proto"
GENERATED_DIR="${WORK_DIR}/dronecode_sdk/generated"
PLUGIN_DIR="${WORK_DIR}/dronecode_sdk/plugins"
PLUGIN_INIT="${PLUGIN_DIR}/__init__.py"
export TEMPLATE_PATH="${WORK_DIR}/other/templates/"

function generate {
    echo -e "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\n" > $PLUGIN_INIT

    for PROTO_FILE in `find ${PROTO_DIR} -name "*.proto" -type f`; do

        # Generate bindings for each file individually
        python3 -m grpc_tools.protoc -I${GENERATED_DIR} \
                                     --proto_path=$(dirname ${PROTO_FILE}) \
                                     --python_out=${GENERATED_DIR} \
                                     --grpc_python_out=${GENERATED_DIR} \
                                     ${PROTO_FILE}

        # For some reason the import is broken with Python3.5.x and works fine
        # with Python3.6.x, set an absolute path and everything is fine
        PROTO_IMPORT_NAME="$(basename -- ${PROTO_FILE%.*})_pb2"

        # We need to create the .original backup files, otherwise we're not compatible with
        # BSD sed.
        sed -i'.sedoriginal' -e "s/import ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME}/from . import ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME}/" \
            "${GENERATED_DIR}/${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME}_grpc.py"
        # Clean up the backup files.
        find ${GENERATED_DIR} -name '*.sedoriginal' -delete
        echo " -> [+] Generated protobuf and gRPC bindings for ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME%_*}"

        # Generate plugin
        python3 -m grpc_tools.protoc -I$(dirname ${PROTO_FILE}) \
                                     --plugin=protoc-gen-custom=$(which dcsdkgen) \
                                     --custom_out=${PLUGIN_DIR} \
                                     --custom_opt=py \
                                     ${PROTO_FILE}

        WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME="$(echo ${PROTO_FILE} | sed "s#.*/\(.*\).proto#\1#g").py"
        # protoc generates java like filenames, we don't want that with python

        # @TODO: cleanup this script and figure out a way to make it cross-os friendly perhaps rewrite in python
        # capilalization as trivial as this needs a workaround for macos bash 3.2
        # this solution avoids using bash ^ substitution (from bash >4.0) and is using python 3 instead
        CAPITALIZED_PLUGIN_NAME=$(python3 -c "import sys;print(sys.argv[1].capitalize())" "$WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME")
        mv ${PLUGIN_DIR}/${CAPITALIZED_PLUGIN_NAME} ${PLUGIN_DIR}/${WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME}
        # Add to imports
        echo "from .${WANTED_PLUGIN_NAME%.py} import *" >> $PLUGIN_INIT
        echo " -> [+] Generated plugin for ${PROTO_IMPORT_NAME%_*}"

    done
}

}

install_dcsdkgen
echo "[+] Done"
echo "[+] Generating plugins from "
generate
echo "[+] Done"

If it's the latter, it would be an API in mavsdk.h, either additional or using the existing intercept as proposed.

PR #2870 implements exactly this — it adds `start_tlog_recording(path)` and `stop_tlog_recording()` directly on the `Mavsdk` class. All incoming MAVLink traffic is recorded with microsecond-precision timestamps in standard .tlog format readable by QGroundControl, Mission Planner, MAVProxy, and pymavlink.

@Ryanf55 sorry, I misunderstood that you wanted to do this and read it as you also wanted it. Feel free to make an implementation, feel free to take @bansiesta's as inspiration.

The example is already up at #2867 — it uses `intercept_incoming_messages_async()` to get raw `mavlink_message_t` structs (solving the parsed-vs-raw-bytes problem) and re-serialises them with `mavlink_msg_to_send_buffer()` before prepending the 8-byte big-endian µs timestamp. Works with QGC / Mission Planner. Happy to hand it off to @Ryanf55 if they want to take it further.

Nice to see an example put together! 
Did you consider how we will handle differentiating which interface packets were on?

Good question — the short answer is: the  spec has no per-packet interface field, so there's no clean way to embed that info in a single file.

A few options for multi-interface setups:

1. **Separate file per connection** — open one tlog writer per `MavlinkPassthrough` connection and name them after the interface (e.g. `udp_14550.tlog`, `serial_0.tlog`). This is probably the most practical approach and what tools like MAVProxy do when recording.
2. **STATUSTEXT marker packets** — inject a synthetic `MAVLINK_MSG_ID_STATUSTEXT` at the start of each interface's stream to label it. Hacky, but survives concatenation.
3. **Accept single-interface** — for the common case (one UDP link to a flight controller) the question doesn't arise, which is what the current example targets.

For the example in #2867, it uses a single connection and doesn't try to solve multi-interface. If determining per-interface origin matters for your router validation use case, option 1 (separate files) would be the most reliable. Happy to extend the example to support that if it would be useful.

comments.body: Do you use futures/promises in your code? Or is this happening in the MAVSDK side?

I do not use any futures in my code. I used a future in the system discovery before (like in the example) but I replaced it with busy waiting to narrow down the problem. 
So it must be on MAVSDK side as I could not imagine any side-effects with ROS2. 
It happens always when the result of `telemetry_->set_rate_battery()` is not success.
I have had this happen too when using the sync functions. It seems to be related to retrying commands

I did some further testing and figured out, that the result is `CommandDenied`before the error occurs. I can't say if the behavior is unique to this result though. 
I am currently testing it in SITL but it also happens when connected to a flight controller. 
To reproduce the described behavior I have a disarmed copter in SITL and restart the software until I get the error. It takes approximately 20 restarts until the error occurs - sometimes even more.
I have seen this happen in CI tests recently as well. Could not track it down yet.

After some investigating I tracked the error down to: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L48-L56 It seems as the first result is a ```CommandDenied``` as mentioned above. However, just a moment later another result of the type ```Success``` is provided. This leads to ```std::future_error: Promise already satisfied```.  During further investigating I found this LogWarn Message in a comment in the ```do_work()``` function, which handles the ```_work_queue```: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L290-L303
After uncommentating the Warning Message I discovered, that the Error always occurs after this Warning was sent. Makes sense, as a the result is set to ```CommandDenied``` in the same if-statement.

After also uncommenting https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L99-L100 and https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L280 one can see these Logging messages:
```
[11:31:25|Debug] Command 511 to send to 1, 1 (mavlink_commands.cpp:99)
[11:31:25|Debug] sending it the first time (511) (mavlink_commands.cpp:280)
[11:31:25|Debug] sending it the first time (511) (mavlink_commands.cpp:280)
[11:31:25|Warn ] A command cannot be sent if another command with the same command_id is still processing! Ignoring command 511 (mavlink_commands.cpp:291)
[11:31:25|Debug] sending it the first time (511) (mavlink_commands.cpp:280)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::future_error'
what():  std::future_error: Promise already satisfied
```

In my opinion this is due to the fact, that ```do_work()``` realizes, that another command with the same ID exists and ignores it but why does it return ```CommandDenied```? Shouldn't it just skip and and during the next iteration (or whenever the previous command with the same ID is done) it takes care of this command?

I tried it by commenting out https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/f4987b17a0f766969efb2593e28d57c2c46c000e/src/core/mavlink_commands.cpp#L295-L300 and setting the rate worked consistently (at least for 100 consecutive tries). During these 100 tries the Warning due to another command with the same ID still being processed occured 8 times, which also leads to the question why this even happens in the first place.

It is expected that the second command receives a `CommandDenied` result. We don't want to retry it later, we delegate that to the user.

Now the thing is that there are two separate commands, and they should use two separate promises. Your bug suggests that maybe there is a confusion somewhere and that both results are sent to the same command :thinking:. Could it be?

> Now the thing is that there are two separate commands, and they should use two separate promises. Your bug suggests that maybe there is a confusion somewhere and that both results are sent to the same command thinking. Could it be?

That's an interesting thought.

@fas2037 do you have easy steps or a setup where it's easier to trigger this?

comments.body:
Rally points are not implemented in MAVSDK, though it could be added.

A first step would be to explain here how that's supposed to work:

* What are the mavlink messages used for that (link to the MAVLink specs on mavlink.io)
* Could that fit in the [mission](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/master/protos/mission/mission.proto) plugin, or should it go in a "RallyPoint" plugin?
* How do we know if the autopilot supports rally points or not? What do we do if we cannot know or if we know it is not supported?

@JonasVautherin The rally point sequence is exactly the same as the [mission protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/mission.html) except that you need to specify a `mission_type` of `MAV_MISSION_TYPE_RALLY` (instead of `MAV_MISSION_TYPE_MISSION`) in most messages and the payload is always [MAV_CMD_NAV_RALLY_POINT](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_RALLY_POINT).

There is a protocol bit you can check for support: [MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY_MISSION_RALLY](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY_MISSION_RALLY).

As to where it should go, the purist in me would like a separate plugin but the pragmatist says in mission plugin. 
- The pragmatist reasoning is that implementation-wise everything is the same, so it is easier development and maintenance. 
- The purist point of view is that conceptually a rally point and a mission are different things that apply in different ways. The fact they are the infrastructure in MAVLink and QGC treats them as part of the same "plan" is an incidental association.

Ups to you.
PS Geofence is also a variation on mission protocol.
We should do some refactoring first and extract the mission protocol stuff (downloading and uploading) mission items into mavsdk and then re-use it in the mission, geofence, and rally plugin.

So do you suggest to create separate plugins?
Conceptually i understand rally points and geofence as part of a mission as they are dependent of the mission items and the concret mission so in some way they go together. It's true that missionItems are different of rallyPoints but for me all of them belongs to a mission.

Interesting take. I haven't thought about this in that way.

To me it's not necessarily connected. For instance I can fly using offboard but still require a geofence.

Yes, you  are right. Depending the vehicle usage it can be thought in a way or another. I was thinking in the way i use the drone as i want to execute fixed missions and for me a mission includes everything. Rally points, geofence, etc. 
For a more generalistic use case probbly has more sense to split this and generate differents plugins though.

Seems like nobody is strongly against having a separate plugin (my understanding is that it is the preferred choice). I would vote for having a `RallyPoint` plugin. It also makes it consistent with the already existing `Mission` and `Geofence` plugins.

@itrigitech would you be willing to start working on that? Feel free to open a draft pull request with whatever you get, even if it is just the header files. So we can comment on the interface :blush:.

Oh, just thought about @julianoes' comment:

> We should do some refactoring first and extract the mission protocol stuff

That's actually true. Now I'm wondering how we would organize that. Have an `src/flightplan` folder that would contain something like:

```
CMakeLists.txt // This builds mission, geofence and rallypoint below
common // This contains the common protocol part
geofence // This is the actual geofence plugin, with its own CMakeLists.txt creating libmavsdk_geofence.so
mission // This is the actual mission plugin, with its own CMakeLists.txt creating libmavsdk_mission.so
rallypoint // This is the actual rallypoint plugin, with its own CMakeLists.txt creating libmavsdk_rallypoint.so
```

What do you guys think?

title: mavlink error when adding a udp connection with port forwarding On
author: SebastianRosewick
body:
Hello!

I would like to connect to the same PX4 sitl instance from multiple processes using an instance of _mavsdk::Mavsdk_.
When i add a udp connection with the option _ForwardingOn_, the terminal with the px4 sitl instance that i tried to connect to is flooded with the warning:
_WARN  [mavlink] ODOMETRY: estimator_type 8 unsupported_

The Mavsdk process also reports:
_MAVLink: critical: ODOMETRY: estimator_type 8 unsupported_

Any help would be much appreciated!
Kinds Regards!
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
There is a difference between:

Listening on a port (on any network interface):
```
udp://:14530
```

Sending UDP to an IP and port:
```
udp://127.0.0.1:14530
```

Also see (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/b87a21d9044b9385e570fe0dd3389b74a3d52c2d/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L78-L81) (@JonasVautherin we need to fix this, people run into it again and again).

So, you need to change one of your two processes to:

```
ConnectionResult connection_result = mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
...
```

Glad I could help! By any chance, do both of your mavsdk instances have the same sysid, compid? I would try to set the configuration custom and vary it, so that you don't end up with conflicts, which is what these retries could be caused by.
242 would be a request for  [HOME_POSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HOME_POSITION).

comments.body:
Are you trying to do anything with odometry?

The error message is generated in PX4 here:
https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/4a553938fb6bc7a853b83d175544fff26b404f68/src/modules/mavlink/mavlink_receiver.cpp#L1484

Hi Julian,

i wasn't trying to do anything with odom, but i think i already found my mistake by falsely forwarding messages between two systems causing the estimator_type error.
My goal was to use the telemetry plugin from two processes to get data from a leader drone.
I guess PX4's remote port can only be used by one mavsdk instance at a time so i tried to write a broadcaster for the leading drone and to use the mavlink-router instead.
Or is there actually a way to use two telemetry plugin instances on the same remote port?

Many thanks for your help!
Sebastian

>  Or is there actually a way to use two telemetry plugin instances on the same remote port?

Hm, why would you need that?
I'm trying to simulate a leader drone with multiple followers that need to receive telemetry data from the leader.

Ok, so the multiple followers are separate MAVLink components, or is it all one process?

If it's the former, you can use [MAVLink forwarding](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/connections.html#forwarding-mavlink-between-connections). And if it is the latter you should be able to just subscribe multiple times to a telemetry subscription.

Hello Julian,

yes, the followers would be separate MAVLink components running as own processes, e.g. on the follower-drones companion computer.
What i understood from the documentation is that port forwarding is used within the same program only?
When i try to connect to the same PX4 remote port (e.g. udp://:14540) from different processes with mavsdk::Mavsdk I always got a bind error:
`bind error: Address already in use (udp_connection.cpp:85)
Connection error: Bind error`

Sorry if Im slow on the uptake here,
Thanks again!

Oh, I see the confusion, no problem.

So what I mean is that you add two connections (or more) and you enable following between them. This means the messages are forwarded to another port, so that an additional MAVLink component (or MAVSDK process) can use it.

You can see an example here:
https://github.com/julianoes/siyi-a8-mini-camera-manager/blob/main/camera-manager/camera_manager.cpp#L73-L83

And to prevent bind errors, you will have to use different ports.

There is a difference between:

Listening on a port (on any network interface):
```
udp://:14530
```

Sending UDP to an IP and port:
```
udp://127.0.0.1:14530
```

Also see (https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/b87a21d9044b9385e570fe0dd3389b74a3d52c2d/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L78-L81) (@JonasVautherin we need to fix this, people run into it again and again).

So, you need to change one of your two processes to:

```
ConnectionResult connection_result = mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
...
```

My bad, it is described very well [here](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/connections.html#behave-like-a-client) in the docs.
What i did now was on the forwarding process:
```
mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://127.0.0.1:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14540", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOn);
```
for a bidirectional connection and on the subscribing process:
```
mavsdk.add_any_connection("udp://:14530", ForwardingOption::ForwardingOff);
```
So the system discovery is forwarded to the other process succesfully.
On the subscribing process however i got errors and warnings looking like this:
```
[02:57:07|Error] Retrying failed (520) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:344)
[02:57:08|Error] Retrying failed (512) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:344)
.
.
.
[02:58:52|Warn ] sending again after 0.509955 s, retries to do: 3  (512). (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:317)
[02:58:52|Warn ] Request was for msg ID: 242 (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:323)
```

So maybe it is better to use ```mavsdk::TelemetryServer``` instead of forwarding the entire mavlink traffic of one system just to create a Telemetry Plugin in a different process?

I was able to get something good enough running for my purposes, so i would feel bad holding you back with this issue any more.
Thanks again for your help and patience!

Glad I could help! By any chance, do both of your mavsdk instances have the same sysid, compid? I would try to set the configuration custom and vary it, so that you don't end up with conflicts, which is what these retries could be caused by.

You're right, after i set ```system_id``` and ```component_id``` explicitly, it did fix the error on the forwarding side.
On the mavsdk instance that is handed the forwarded connection i still get errors for msg 242:

```
[01:44:22|Warn ] Request was for msg ID: 242 (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:323)
[01:44:22|Error] Retrying failed (512) (mavlink_command_sender.cpp:344)
```
So the subscriber to the forwarded connection is requested to send a [MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_SET_SENSOR_OFFSETS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_PREFLIGHT_SET_SENSOR_OFFSETS), which it keeps failing to send?
Both Configuration Types are set to ```ComponentType::Custom```

In the mean time i set up a ```TelemetryServer``` instead and it is working without problems so far.
242 would be a request for  [HOME_POSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HOME_POSITION).
Closing this. Comment again if it's still unclear.
Yes, this can be closed. Sorry for the late reply and thank you again very much!

title: ArduPilot - Problem identified that may be causing the mission module to fail (fly_mission example)
author: trolledbypro
body:
Hello, I have found a possible cause of this issue of the mission module failing in ArduPilot. 
Using Wireshark, I analyzed the network traffic between my ArduPilot SITL (running inside a WSL2 Docker container that runs the latest ArduPilot Docker image) and the MAVSDK example (running inside WSL2 as I was having issues running it in Windows 10). My MAVSDK library and my fly_mission binary were built in _debug_ mode using CMake through CMake Tools in VSCode (using VSCode WSL Remote session).

Here is my terminal output:  
![image](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/57928210/31595d2e-923d-4817-aeea-85eb264c2683)

There is a debug message saying the gimbal version is v1, and that the mission is unsupported.
Examining Wireshark, the last message sent before the MISSION_ACK message containing the MAV_MISSION_UNSUPPORTED payload was MAV_CMD_DO_MOUNT_CONFIGURE (204). 

When gimbal angles are defined in a mission_item, the gimbal version is verified: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L460
We then use the version above and send a version specific message containing the gimbal configuration. Below, we see that the unsupported message is sent if the gimbal version is assumed to be v1, as is the case in my console output:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/fadfe22e7c053945107201e2638be9a7f8b8ee5c/src/mavsdk/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L1188-L1221

It appears that MAVSDK is not finding out the supported gimbal version. Gimbal v1 is deprecated in ArduPilot as of version 4.3. Wireshark shows that no GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION (280) messages were sent from the AP and no MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE (512) message from MAVSDK requesting the gimbal version was sent. The GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION message is what the gimbal module uses to set the gimbal version.

I propose the following two solutions. I think the latter is more inclusive to more ArduPilot versions but the former could be implemented quicker:
- default to v2 if ArduPilot is detected
- send a request for GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION if ArduPilot is detected

What do you all think?

Thanks @trolledbypro for looking into this! :rocket: 

I think I would be in favour of a third version: drop gimbal v1 entirely and always assume v2. There are many problems with the detection anyway.

One that I learn here is that the `mission` module needs to know about the gimbal protocol, so either we need to duplicate the detection that [we already have in the `gimbal` module](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/gimbal/gimbal_impl.cpp#L58-L62), or we need the `mission` module to depend on the `gimbal` one somehow (which we have never done with any plugin before).

But on top of that, the detection we have in the `gimbal` module is fundamentally flawed (and the root cause is in the MAVLink design): MAVLink does not offer a mechanism to differentiate between a timeout and an unsupported message (many modules just ignore commands they don't support, and the MAVLink specs allow a broadcast command which require this behavior). So we can be sure that a drone supports Gimbal v2 when everything works ("yay I received a v2 message, I know it supports v2"), but we can never be sure that it does not support v2 ("I did not receive a v2 message, is it because the drone does not support v2, or is it because the messages were lost?"). We could probably do more convoluted heuristics (like "I got 3 timeouts for the gimbal v2 requests while I received X messages from the drone, so I will say that I am reasonably confident that it was not a timeout"), but... well is it worth it?

I don't know of a single drone that uses Gimbal v1, and v2 has been out there for years. Maybe it is time to drop v1 entirely.
