So, is this fix good enough for you?

title: Who should initiate TIMESYNC?
author: JonasVautherin
body:
This is related to #1169. Looking at MAVSDK's timesync implementation, it seems like we send TIMESYNC messages in two situations:

1. In `process_timesync`, where we receive a TIMESYNC message and answer to it
2. In `do_work`, where we actually initiate the TIMESYNC exchange

Is it meant to be like this, or do different components have different needs? E.g. the "master" (I would guess the autopilot) could be the one initiating the sync, and he other components may or may not answer depending on their needs, right?

@irsdkv: your insights would be appreciated :slightly_smiling_face:!
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
> please say why this is a problem to save this functionality enabled by default?

Because it's not clear to me how TIMESYNC supports more than 2 components doing the synchronization. Hence, if you have more than 2 components, I'm currently assuming that you will have to disable TIMESYNC in the extra ones, and you will have to know which one needs to enable it. In that case, it seems more legit to have it disabled by default IMO.

My reasoning is the following: the TIMESYNC message is a broadcast message (because it doesn't have `target_system` and `target_component`). Therefore, a component cannot know who the message was destined to. So if you have, say, the FCU synchronizing with a module M1 on the companion, and at the same time a module M2 on the companion synchronizing with the ground station, then I can't imagine how the FCU can make the difference between the response coming from M1 (which it is interested in) and the response coming from the ground station (which is destined to M2).

@AlexisTM Yes. There is a little discussion of this message here: https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink-devguide/issues/194#issuecomment-512037079

And one day I will find time to document it.
I would vote that we make this feature opt-in for use cases where it is required, and supported.
Ok, that answers my question, and TIMESYNC is now disabled by default in MAVSDK. Closing this.

comments.body:
This is the same implementation as in MAVROS:

For the FCU to sync, the FCU sends a message and waits for the onboard computer to answer.
For the onboard computer to sync, it sends a message and waits for the FCU's answer.

This could be in tri-way protocol two-way, where the onboard computer sends a request, FCU replies and the onboard answers to the FCU. The onboard computer will have its sync from the 2 first messages, the FCU from the 3 last messages. This would remove one message but add one time to the TIMESYNC message. I do not know it would improve bandwidth.
Mavros implementation:

[Replies]
https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/de9f39a719b091b8448214a17d27b3b1c415d0dc/mavros/src/plugins/sys_time.cpp#L308-L321

[Requests]
https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/de9f39a719b091b8448214a17d27b3b1c415d0dc/mavros/src/plugins/sys_time.cpp#L334-L346


Precision Time Protocol 2: [NOT PX4's version]
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6976744/90625099-59fc7b00-e219-11ea-8277-8522f899d45d.png)

Oh it was a long time ago and unfortunately I don't remember all important details now :(

But @AlexisTM explanation is correct.

Also I would to say that [this code change](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1169/files#diff-ec4205b6bc1adbc844894d870f234adaR9) disables ability to answer to `TIMESYNC` requests from other devices in common with disabling MAVSDK's own requests.

I think that it is a good idea to save the opportunity to sync time by default in case of other device want to do it.

What are you think about that, @AlexisTM ?

UPD:
Also I think that disabling by default MAVSDK's initiated timesync is not a bad idea, because it is needed only for positioning using external vision for now as I know.

I am personally not using MAVSDK at the moment.

But indeed, it would make sense to have it disabled by default as only experienced users make use offboard control and need Timesync.
If the user uses advanced functions, I would either auto-enable timesync or give a feedback that timesync is not enabled and should for advanced usage. (advanced usage would be offboard control or external vision)

I checked out #1034 and found that it is only way to disable `do_work` and `process_timesync` both simultaneously.

And as @AlexisTM said this functionality really needed only for advanced usage.

So this PR seems like a good choice.

But @JonasVautherin please say why this is a problem to save this functionality enabled by default? Is it add payload or brings some other troubles?

> please say why this is a problem to save this functionality enabled by default?

Because it's not clear to me how TIMESYNC supports more than 2 components doing the synchronization. Hence, if you have more than 2 components, I'm currently assuming that you will have to disable TIMESYNC in the extra ones, and you will have to know which one needs to enable it. In that case, it seems more legit to have it disabled by default IMO.

My reasoning is the following: the TIMESYNC message is a broadcast message (because it doesn't have `target_system` and `target_component`). Therefore, a component cannot know who the message was destined to. So if you have, say, the FCU synchronizing with a module M1 on the companion, and at the same time a module M2 on the companion synchronizing with the ground station, then I can't imagine how the FCU can make the difference between the response coming from M1 (which it is interested in) and the response coming from the ground station (which is destined to M2).

@JonasVautherin I fully agree, this protocol was designed out of necessity for a time synchronization between two devices to allow better control. 

I believe it is useless in most of the use-cases and instead will be a problem to the user if multiple endpoints are connected.

TIMESYNC only works if:
* There are **only** two devices
* The synchronization time is computed & filtered in **each** receiving end (the pixhawk for vision estimation input & the computer for position output)
* The link should be high speed with low jitter, probably only using hardware serial (USB-Serial has up to 20ms spikes)

@AlexisTM Yes. There is a little discussion of this message here: https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink-devguide/issues/194#issuecomment-512037079

And one day I will find time to document it.
I would vote that we make this feature opt-in for use cases where it is required, and supported.
Ok, that answers my question, and TIMESYNC is now disabled by default in MAVSDK. Closing this.

title: When running MAVSDK against ArduCopter SITL the Action/goto_location function always responds with Command Denied
author: paulholmstedt
body: I'm running a software based on latest MAVSDK code i.e. I built library on Windows 64-bit from Main branch on GitHub. I'm using two different ArduCopter SITL, one running on Linux and one directly on a Cube Orange autopilot. So far I've tested take-off, landing, MissionRaw and Offboard mode using a gamepad. All working pretty good after some tweeks. The problem is the goto_location and goto_location_async functions which always return Command Denied no matter what I do. The command is issued when ArduCopter is in "Hold" mode in the air i.e. UAV keeping its current position. Do you have any suggestion why these MAVSDK functions might not work together with ArduCopter?

answer_comments.body: In that case, let's switch to guided mode if ArduPilot. Good find @paulholmstedt!

@paulholmstedt: would you be willing to open a PR with that change? I guess we need to discriminate between px4 and ardupilot, and switch to guided if ardupilot (as Julian suggested). Another example where we do that kind of discrimination is [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L260-L264), for inspiration :blush:.

Would you like to try?

I might have found another bug in `goto_location_async`: MAVSDK sends a CommandInt but the Frame (WGS84) might not be set correctly. According to the function documentation you give it a absolute altitude (WGS84) but ArduPilot interpret the altitude as a relative altitude instead of a WGS84 altitude. So when I call `goto_location_async` I need to subtract the launch position WGS84 altitude prior to calling the function. After that the function works correctly. Looking at the code the CommanInt is set to `MAV_FRAME frame = MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT;`
I will try the "git e-mail workflow" way :-)

Here is a patch file for my changes. I hope I got it right :-)

title: Intermittent issue of all gimbal control erroring with Pixy LR gimbal
author: jnomikos
body:
~~From my experience, MAVSDK does not detect a system is lost on soft reboot. Which is fine for most things I am doing. camera_server, param, and mavlink_passthrough seem to work fine for me even after the soft reboot.~~

~~The problem is that gimbal does not work after the reboot. Giving any gimbal control after soft rebooting will result in a failure to do so, with it returning the result as "Error". ~~

~~My assumption is that MAVSDK still thinks it has control of the gimbal, when it doesn't, since it did not know the autopilot was rebooted. I am not able to make it so that MAVSDK detects reboots, even if I increase BRD_BOOT_DELAY. 
In my application, this will be fine, because I have a background thread that detects when we last received telemetry position, so I can use that to detect a reboot, but I still wanted to make an issue here, just to give a heads up of the issue I found.~~



System:

MAVSDK v3.2.0
ArduCopter 4.5.6
Pixy LR gimbal

Note: MAVSDK is connected to flight controller via UART



**Edit:**

I fixed this issue. The problem was not due to rebooting.

The Pixy LR gimbal sends GIMBAL_MANAGER messages from comp id 154 and the autopilot sends GIMBAL_MANAGER messages from comp id 1. I hard coded MAVSDK to completely ignore comp id 154 and the intermittent problem is gone. 

As a note, it would constantly request GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION from 1/154. I know MAVSDK has a retries mechanism, but it didn't seem to stop this. So my hardcoding got rid of that.

I would vote to make the example rather minimal, so you would not expose all of the config options but just give the most  obvious use case.

Yes, though it would be good if it could emulate "proper usage" of a location source. By which I mean that if the sources are normally asynchronous callbacks whenever new data arrives, it would be good to show how to write an app that works with that kind of source.

title: Log download via udp over ethernet stalls
author: nickatblueflite
body:
Hardware Setup: Holybro 6X <- eth -> Jetson Xavier

Using the code out of the logfile_download.py example I have no trouble downloading the full set of files with a serial connection.

However, when connecting over an eth connection downloads will start fine then always stall and never recover. 

In fact, the "connection" goes down fully and the only way to reconnect is to reboot the pix. I've run the mavsdk_server manually to watch its output and the only thing that happens is the heartbeats timed out message appears and then nothing.

The connection seems stable otherwise and works well when using mavlink-router to forward to a GCS over the network.

answer_comments.body:
> 10.223.129.101 is the Jetson, 10.223.129.102 is the pixhawk

So it looks like there is also 10.223.129.103 and all traffic is forwarded to that one. Not sure if that matters or not, but does it also happen without that forwarding on?

> I don't even know where to begin to look into that...

Neither. I never had to look into the NuttX network stack so far.

This would be a start: https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/NUTTX/Networking
This is likely fixed with #2654. For me, the loopback UDP buffer overflowed because PX4 sends too much at once.

title: Choosing reference over pointer
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
It is recommended to use references when we can, and pointers when we have to.
(Reference: https://isocpp.org/wiki/faq/references#refs-vs-ptrs)

We can replace `Device *_parent` to `Device & _parent` as I see that, its possible. We initialize while activating plugin and never modify it. Also, we have a method (below) that actually gives, **a reference to a device**, not pointer. 
```cpp
Device &device(uint64_t uuid);
```

Consider, below piece of application code:
```cpp
Device &device = dc.device(); // we get reference to device
auto action = std::make_shared<Action>(&device); // why pass its address ?

// Why not pass it as-is?
auto action = std::make_shared<Action>(device);
```
I just noticed this.
@julianoes, was it done intentionally for some vital reason? If not, then we can find similar usages and replace them properly.

answer_comments.body: I tend to agree. Thanks for writing that up @shakthi-prashanth-m. Do you agree @JonasVautherin?
Yes, I agree. I usually use references and smart pointers instead of raw pointers.

   - not that doc build doesn't work on windows anyway right now. 

So, suggestion:
1. Make system install the default
   - If someone does this build on windows fail and display a message "System install not supported on windows - do `THE COMMAND to build locally`
2. Make docs build against system install path (doxygen config file change). On Windows fail the docs call with a message that"Automated docs builds not supported on Windows".
3. Example code has to stay the same - that should build on windows too.
4. Docs change to separate out how you can point to local installs as a separate topic.
Thoughts?
Ok, I support the suggestion.
@julianoes Awseome - do you need me to create an issue report?
Done in #73.

I think it is against PX4: "Serial interface between the PX4 and RPI."

But it is a rover :innocent:.

@ssarfati: Actually, are you sure that you are using PX4 and not Ardupilot? It is not clear to me if Mission Planner works with PX4. Note that "PX4" is not the same thing as "Pixhawk". You could be running Ardupilot on a Pixhawk, and that would not be PX4 :blush:.

Ok, good to know :-). So I'm closing this for now, since it's not a connection issue between MAVSDK and PX4 :innocent:.

About the configuration for the rover, I would suggest you ask in #rover on the PX4 Slack! :blush:
Yes, rover support is very basic in PX4, and I'm not sure how well MAVSDK works with PX4 rover.

```
    func uploadMission(){
        let cancelMissionUploadRoutine =
            CoreManager.shared().drone.mission.cancelMissionUpload()
                .do(onError: { (error) in
                    print("Error canceling mission upload \(error)")
                }, onCompleted: {
                    print("Success canceling mission upload.")
                })
        
        let uploadMissionRoutine =
            CoreManager.shared().drone.mission.uploadMission(missionItems: missionExample.missionItems)
            .do(onError: { error in
                self.displayFeedback(message:"Mission uploaded failed \(error)")
                
            }, onCompleted: {
                self.displayFeedback(message:"Mission uploaded with success")
            })
                
       let uploadRoutine = cancelMissionUploadRoutine.andThen(uploadMissionRoutine)
        uploadRoutine
            .subscribeOn(SerialDispatchQueueScheduler(qos: .background))
            .observeOn(MainScheduler.instance)
            .subscribe()
            .disposed(by: disposeBag)
    }
```

Should I try a local install and see if the mavsdk.dll can be found there?

[This](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L94) is (I believe) where we say where the library should be installed. On Linux it gets into `lib/` (more specifically `lib/libmavsdk.so`, `lib/libmavsdk.so.0`, `lib/libmavsdk.so.0.50.1`).

Could you try to debug it? For instance, you could try to print `${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}` [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L94) to see if it looks correct on Windows. With something like:

title: Changing from offboard mode to mission mode
author: MrPrietix
body:
Hi 

I am loading a mission to the drone, then I am starting offboard mode and when it has reached an altitude I change to mission mode, these changes of different modes are done with an onboard computer. All of this is performed without the RC connected. Furthermore, the arming is done with the onboard computer. 

Nevertheless, when the drone changes to mission mode, it wants to reach a higher altitude different that the initial 5 meters specified on QGC when designing the mission. When it comes to the mission mode I am just running the `MissionRaw::Result start_mission_result = mission_raw->start_mission();` without loading any mission with mavsdk. I am supposing that when I run `MissionRaw::Result start_mission_result = mission_raw->start_mission();` the drone automatically takes the mission in the flight controller.

Can anybody help me?

answer_comments.body:
The waypoints are saved in the Autopilot, MAVSDK cannot change them without re-uploading the mission (in which case you could download it from QGC and see that the altitude changed).

> All of this is performed without the RC connected.

Are you sure the drone doesn't just go to RTL as a failsafe? To me that would explain why it gains altitude :thinking:

I was guessing an RC loss, but really I don't know. I just don't see how MAVSDK would change the mission altitude. It's not really a thing: mission items ("waypoints") are uploaded to PX4, and then when you tell PX4 to go in `mission` mode, it executes them. MAVSDK should put PX4 in mission mode just like QGC does :thinking:.

I guess my question was: are you sure that it is in mission mode, or could it be in another mode (like RTL, which is a mode that could start by gaining altitude in some situations)

Just while looking at your log I saw that [thrust correlates with your mag](https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=0d0df6e7-1248-495d-9a1d-67cd14af68e1#Nav-Thrust-and-Magnetic-Field) which means that you mean is too close to your power wiring or motors. I'd suggest using a GPS mast, or if you're already doing that, make sure that the external mag in the GPS board is used.

---
Now that aside, if you look at the [altitude plot](https://logs.px4.io/plot_app?log=0d0df6e7-1248-495d-9a1d-67cd14af68e1#Nav-Altitude-Estimate) you can see that it sets a altitude setpoint at around 175m (this tiny yellow circle), and then climbs to it.

My assumption is that this is really the mission you set it to. Can you show the mission that you set? E.g. the QGC mission plan file, or a screenshot of it. I would be interested in the altitude that you set, as well as the frame. Unfortunately, the mission is not logged to ulog, so I can't see that.

I'm confused. I'm looking at a plan with 2 items and a doJumpId of 2 and 3 respectively. I don't even know how this works. The altitude itself looks like just 5m for both of them.

> they created a takeoff item that does not send the takeoff command but sends the altitude to be taken into consideration during the takeoff.

I don't know how you are doing that but I would guess something is wrong with that.

Or to put it differently: you are telling me that you are doing some magic with the mission items but the altitude is not correct but you also don't actually show me in detail what you're doing so I can't really help.

The reason is that my team removed the default takeoff, but when configuring the mission, they created a takeoff item that does not send the takeoff command but sends the altitude to be taken into consideration during the takeoff. Could it be the doJumpId the problem?
Nevertheless, in simulation, everything works perfectly.

Regarding the frame, it is the Quadrotor X.
[mission_plan_custom.txt](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/files/9130317/mission_plan_custom.txt)

I'm confused. I'm looking at a plan with 2 items and a doJumpId of 2 and 3 respectively. I don't even know how this works. The altitude itself looks like just 5m for both of them.

> they created a takeoff item that does not send the takeoff command but sends the altitude to be taken into consideration during the takeoff.

I don't know how you are doing that but I would guess something is wrong with that.

Or to put it differently: you are telling me that you are doing some magic with the mission items but the altitude is not correct but you also don't actually show me in detail what you're doing so I can't really help.
By using a default mission file without our modifications it works. So it is solved. Nevertheless, thank you.

body:

title: Mission generation should use NAV_DELAY instead of sending two waypoints on the same location
author: LorenzMeier
body:
From @julianoes:
> The reason MAVSDK sends the same lat/lon twice in a row is because it adds a LOITER_TIME right after a NAV_WAYPOINT. The right approach would be to use NAV_DELAY [...].

Which is implemented in PX4 for quite some time (I verified). The reason PX4 rejects now waypoints that are on top of each other is because the path between those waypoints is not defined (zero distance). Often we however need to know where the vehicle is coming from geometrically and allowing N waypoints on the same location would force us to traverse the mission multiple times and quite a bit forward and backward, increasing the complexity of the autopilot in terms of memory, execution time and also in terms of our ability to QA and certify the code.

So in short: This is undesirable in principle and navigation commands should not exist in the same physical location one after the other.

answer_comments.body:
> So in short: This is undesirable in principle and navigation commands should not exist in the same physical location one after the other.

If this is a hard rule it should also be added to the MAVLink standard.
@dayjaby I suppose for this case we should be using WAYPOINT, DELAY, IMAGE_START_CAPTURE, DELAY, but maybe that's not possible given the current implementation.

comments.body:
> So in short: This is undesirable in principle and navigation commands should not exist in the same physical location one after the other.

If this is a hard rule it should also be added to the MAVLink standard.

There are a couple of scenarios that cannot be done if there is such a hard rule:
(PREVIOUS WAYPOINT), WAYPOINT, DELAY, IMAGE_START_CAPTURE, LOITER_UNLIMITED for example if the waypoint and loiter_unlimited have the same position. We could prevent this reverse transversing if all the mission items in such a sequence would have the same PREVIOUS WAYPOINT assigned.
@dayjaby I suppose for this case we should be using WAYPOINT, DELAY, IMAGE_START_CAPTURE, DELAY, but maybe that's not possible given the current implementation.
If NAV_DELAY is supported in PX4, is there something preventing this from being implemented? Or can I take a crack at it (time permitting)?
@coderkalyan feel free :)

title: Assets missing files
author: ytyisme
body: [mavsdk-windows-x64.zip](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v3.17.0/mavsdk-windows-x64.zip)is missing mavsdk_export.h

answer_comments.body:
I downloaded and inspected the v3.17.0 zip directly. `mavsdk_export.h` **is present**:

```
include/mavsdk/mavsdk_export.h   ← present
```

`MAVSDKConfig.cmake` sets `INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES` to both `${MAVSDK_ROOT_DIR}/include` and `${MAVSDK_ROOT_DIR}/include/mavsdk`, so the file is reachable as either `#include <mavsdk/mavsdk_export.h>` or `#include <mavsdk_export.h>`. No shipped header references a `.hpp` extension — the `.hpp` rename was only on `main` and was never backported to v3.

Could you clarify what exact error you're seeing? Are you getting a compiler error like `cannot open include file: 'mavsdk/mavsdk_export.h'`, or something else? It's possible the zip download was incomplete/corrupted — re-downloading and re-extracting might help.

One unrelated cmake oddity I noticed: `MAVSDKTargets.cmake` has `${_IMPORT_PREFIX}/include/mavsdk` repeated ~38 times in `INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES` (one entry per target, all duplicated). This is harmless since the Windows dual-config code in `MAVSDKConfig.cmake` builds the target manually and overrides it anyway, but it's worth cleaning up.

Thanks for sharing the zip — that makes it clear. I downloaded your uploaded zip and compared it against the official [v3.17.0 `mavsdk-windows-x64.zip`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v3.17.0/mavsdk-windows-x64.zip) from the Releases page:

| | Official v3.17.0 | Your zip |
|---|---|---|
| `include/mavsdk/mavsdk_export.h` | ✅ present | ❌ missing |
| All other files | identical | identical |

The official release zip does contain `mavsdk_export.h`. Your zip is missing exactly that one file, which suggests you may have downloaded from a mirror, a build artifact, or an older/interim release rather than directly from the GitHub Releases page.

**Fix**: Download the zip fresh from the official Releases page:  
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v3.17.0/mavsdk-windows-x64.zip

Re-extracting that should give you `include/mavsdk/mavsdk_export.h` and resolve the build error.

I just re-downloaded the official `mavsdk-windows-x64.zip` from the v3.17.0 Releases page and inspected it:

```
include/mavsdk/mavsdk_export.h   ✅ present
```

The release asset itself is intact. The first S3 URL in your comment (`objects.githubusercontent.com/github-production-repository-file-5c1aeb/94815442/26742795`) is actually the file *you uploaded* to this issue thread — it's a GitHub user attachment, not the official release download. That's likely the source of the discrepancy.

The second URL (`release-assets.githubusercontent.com/…`) is a correct signed release asset URL, but those temporary links expire after a few minutes, so re-downloading via that URL after it expires can fail silently.

title: [Rtk] Data above 180 bytes length not working
author: Katawann
body:
Hi,

I tested the new RTK plugin and it works like a charm ! Thank you @julianoes for the job.

In my working setup I have something like this:
Ntrip caster <---> Internet <---> Linux Ubuntu 20.04 <---> C++ app with MAVSDK and Ntrip Client <---> USB <---> Pixhawk 4

I noticed that if I send a data with length of 4*180 bytes (accepted by the plugin) it will never turn to RTK position, but sending 180 bytes works fine. Not sure to understand the logic around the fragment ID. Maybe the plugin should only accept 180 bytes maximum or is there a logic I missed ?

answer_comments.body:
The maximum length of the mavlink payload is 255 bytes. Not sure what happens if you write 4*180=720 bytes into the message (that would happen here: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/rtk/rtk_impl.cpp#L60), but I guess if it doesn't crash, maybe it's just ignoring whatever is exceeding.

My feeling is that the rtk plugin should check the length of the data and return an error if it's bigger than 180 (which is what is specified here: https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GPS_RTCM_DATA

Oh, I misread the code, sorry :see_no_evil:. The specs read:

> RTCM message (may be fragmented)

And the code is apparently trying to split the data in multiple messages. So that's something to debug indeed :+1:.

To me it feels like [this line](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/rtk/rtk_impl.cpp#L60) is wrong, as it always sends `rtcm_data.data.c_str()`, and it should instead take the right part of it for each message.

title: Exposing Flight mode APIs in core/device_impl.h
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
We have [methods](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/core/device_impl.h#L86-L89) in `DeviceImpl` for PX4 param get/set; but we don't have methods to know/change flight mode in `DeviceImpl`. These methods are useful for plugins. 

Below are the plugins each of which maps to a **PX4 flight mode**:
- [Offboard plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/offboard/offboard_impl.cpp#L48)
- [FollowMe plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/core/device_impl.h#L86-L89)
- [Mission plugin](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/mission/mission_impl.cpp#L682)

As of now (in above plugins), we're doing the hard way by using  `MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE`. I think it makes sense to expose a method for the same as part of `DeviceImpl` interface. 

At present we've a [public API to get flight mode](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/telemetry/telemetry.h#L392) is part of `Telemetry `plugin. If other plugins want to know flight mode, they can't call `Telemetry` plugin API (which creates plugin dependency). So it is suitable and intuitive to move some of the useful flight mode APIs from `Telemetry` plugin to `Device` as well.

answer_comments.body:
Having this in the `DeviceImpl` for plugins makes sense to me. I would keep the public API in telemetry -
 that is where I would expect to look for it as an API user.
So the answer is Yes. Feel free to close  - and add the functionality/or change this to an issue and keep open.

title: Dronecore as subproject
author: Stifael
body: If dronecore is used as a subproject, in order to compile correctly with the correct paths, each plugin and core requires `target_include_directories(dronecore PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})`, otherwise the header files will not be found.

answer_comments.body:
This has the drawback that also internal header files within a plugin would be public.
E.g. for the action plugin, `action.h` should be public but `action_impl.h` should not.

Another way would be to install the plugin header files in a `plugins` subdirectory. That way the installed directory structure would be closer to the non-installed one.

The change would be to install it as:
```
dronecore/plugins/action/action.h
```
instead of:
```
dronecore/action.h
```

title: Adding disconnect button to kill/disconnect to any port or kill not used variables.
author: AldoCF96
body: I saw that QgroundControl has disconnect button to kill all the connections to a drone in a port. There should be a way to do it in, using MAVSDK, that keeps the code running but just disconnect specifics ports.
resolution_evidence: maintainer points at the fix: 'supported with #2079'

answer_comments.body:
@Macf41 contributions would be very welcome!

So the first thing that we have to think through, in my eyes, is what the API would look like. So, what would the interface be to tell MAVSDK to "remove" a connection? That part is not clear to me just yet.

Deleting/clearing systems is tricky because it involves the plugins being deleted first. Or plugins would only be given a weak_ptr to their system, and before doing anything, they would always have to check if the system is still there with `weak_ptr->lock()`. That's a bit of an overhead that I was trying to avoid so far.

> Either that or we can exposed connections vector so developers can delete any connection they don't need.

Yes, that should be more doable.

comments.body: That sounds reasonable. Do you have a use-case for it?

When handling connections with multiple drones, it would be good to have a way to disconnect to a drone and kill all unused variables, just for a specific connection to a drone. But mavsdk can still be running accepting other connections. Just like Qgc does it.
Right, that makes sense. Would you be willing to contribute that?
Thanks for the issue @AldoCF96.
@JonasVautherin  I can work on that, unless anybody else is working on that. I will need to make research on how mavsdk handle the connections and the auto-discover.

Awesome!

To give you some context, that is done in the `Mavsdk` classes (`mavsdk.h/cpp`, `mavsdk_impl.h/cpp`). Mavsdk opens a connection and then listens for heartbeats. Whenever it receives new heartbeats, it checks if it already knows the sysid or not. If it doesn't, it creates a new `System` for that new sysid.

I guess that you don't want to destroy a `System` if its connection disappears, because a `System` can be present over multiple connections (multipath). So those are two different things: if a `System` is disconnected for too long, maybe it should be removed (but maybe we don't care because we never have so many systems anyway). But in your case I believe you want a way to remove the connection, independently from the system (heartbeat stuff) logic.

title: REQUEST_MESSAGE vs custom getters like REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION
author: JonasVautherin
body:
It's currently part of the [list for MAVSDK v2](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2002), and though I don't think I can contribute an implementation, I think I can contribute a (relatively informed) opinion.

TL;DR: I don't think this can go in MAVSDK v2 :see_no_evil:.

#### We cannot detect what the receiver supports

There is no way to detect if the receiver supports `REQUEST_MESSAGE`, because the requested message could have been requested by someone else, or it could be transmitted spontaneously by the receiver. So making statistics to try to guess stuff like "was this `CAMERA_INFORMATION` message an answer to my request, or is it a coincidence?" is probably not worth it by far.

Also each message is independent. So even if we managed to detect that `REQUEST_MESSAGE` is supported for `CAMERA_INFORMATION`, it would not say anything about e.g. `REQUEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

#### What we can do

* Push the receivers to support both messages (i.e. the drone should support both `REQUEST_MESSAGE(<camera_information>)` and `REQUEST_CAMERA_INFORMATION`.
* Keep the old way in MAVSDK until we feel like we can completely drop it.

In other words, the implementation work is not on the MAVSDK side, but on the receiver side (e.g. make sure that PX4/Ardupilot support the newer messages, make sure that cameras do, push proprietary players to do it).

Some day, maybe we will feel comfortable in dropping the old way and telling people "well if your drone does not support the new way, that's your problem".

answer_comments.body:
> But I see many problems there

Yes, there are many problems. But at some point switching and saying we don't support the old way also doesn't work and also has problems. So my idea is to try hard and do a best effort solution that - while having corner cases - generally works.

> For instance, it is legal to broadcast the command and expect multiple systems/components to broadcast their message.

Yes, it gets indeed tricky with multiple systems and components, so let's only use these commands to specific sysid/compid pairs and not use broadcast.

> Should we somehow keep a state in MAVSDK that says "I am pretty sure that this drone supports the new message because I got an answer once"?

I think you're missing something here. A success is not if we receive the message that we asked for but we receive the ack *AND* the message. That's a definite confirmation that it worked.

> A success is not if we receive the message that we asked for but we receive the ack

Oh, that's a good point! It is a command, so it will be acked in case of success, and therefore you can detect a success (but not all failures: a timeout is indistinguishable from an unsupported command).

So I think you're right: you can probably try both until one (or both) is acked, and when it is, keep it (or keep the new one if both are supported). Or of course if it is UNSUPPORTED then fallback to the other.

> So what about switching to the new REQUEST_MESSAGE command and if it gets UNSUPPORTED, FAILED or a timeout, then we fall back to the old one?

I don't think that is entirely correct. If you have a timeout, you cannot conclude anything, so you should not fall back. I think it's better to try both messages until an answer (SUCCESS/UNSUPPORTED/FAILED) is received, rather than trying the new one for an arbitrary number of seconds and blocking everything during that time in case only the old one is supported.

> A success is [when] we receive the ack AND the message

Hmm I think the ack is enough to detect that the message is supported, no need to deal with the message (which again will be a mess because the message is unreliable and can be sent for many other reasons).

IMO the code in MAVSDK should always handle those messages as "unreliable, spontaneous messages", but MAVSDK can request them separately if it wants to encourage the drone to send it. Thanks for bringing this up. Let's talk through it and make a decision.

My question is: Wouldn't a receiver that doesn't support `REQUEST_MESSAGE` nack it and therefore tell you that it doesn't support it?

> Wouldn't a receiver that doesn't support REQUEST_MESSAGE nack it

I don't think so :thinking:. One problem with MAVLink is that the specs do not require to  nack unsupported messages. I am pretty sure I have seen implementations that just ignore unsupported messages (resulting in a timeout, indistinguishable from an actual timeout in a sane way IMO).

So same thing there: one would have to make it a requirement to nack unsupported messages, ask implementations to change to that, and in a few years when we are fairly sure that all the implementations we care about do it, we could rely on nacks :innocent:.

So actually UNSUPPORTED is for a command that is not supported but not necessarily for a command param that is not supported. So, in that case, it should probably be failed. I would argue a decent camera implementation would do that, rather than timing out.

So what about switching to the new REQUEST_MESSAGE command and if it gets UNSUPPORTED, FAILED or a timeout, then we fall back to the old one?
This means that old implementations would still work, just slower, while new ones will work nicely, and quickly. What am I missing?

I wish it worked, and maybe I'm being too pessimistic. But I see many problems there :see_no_evil:.

> I would argue a decent camera implementation would do that

My understanding of the specs is that it is legal to timeout. For instance, it is legal to broadcast the command and expect multiple systems/components to broadcast their message. I suppose it would be rational to not have all the components return UNSUPPORTED in that case. The specs clearly mention the broadcast possibility : "Request the target **system(s)** emit a single instance of a specified message".

> What am I missing?

Say the drone only supports the new message, and does not time out for unsupported commands. Say the request happens to timeout. What do we do? If we fallback to the old message, it will always time out. Should we then fallback again to the new message? Should we somehow keep a state in MAVSDK that says "I am pretty sure that this drone supports the new message because I got an answer once"? Then we need that logic for every message we request (because the drone could use some of the new messages, and some of the old ones), and we should consider resetting that state if the drone is disconnected/reconnected (because we don't really know if it is the same drone or a different one).

On top of that, what do we do if the detection logic fails? Say MAVSDK requests a message using the new way, and receives an answer. It could totally be that it is a coincidence (the drone decided to send that message at this time/some other GCS requested it at the same time). So MAVSDK will think "oh great, it supports the new message", and maybe it does not. What do we do then?
Actually, maybe one thing we could do is always use both from MAVSDK. I think that could work :thinking:.

> Actually, maybe one thing we could do is always use both from MAVSDK. I think that could work thinking.

Well thinking more about that, it is actually quite useless. Because it does not change the fact that drones should support both (on the contrary, it duplicates messages for nothing).

Again: once we decide that the supported drones all moved to the new message, it makes sense to drop the old messages in MAVSDK and use the new ones. But before that, I really don't see a solution to sanely detect what is supported.

> But I see many problems there

Yes, there are many problems. But at some point switching and saying we don't support the old way also doesn't work and also has problems. So my idea is to try hard and do a best effort solution that - while having corner cases - generally works.

> For instance, it is legal to broadcast the command and expect multiple systems/components to broadcast their message.

Yes, it gets indeed tricky with multiple systems and components, so let's only use these commands to specific sysid/compid pairs and not use broadcast.

> Should we somehow keep a state in MAVSDK that says "I am pretty sure that this drone supports the new message because I got an answer once"?

Hmm I think the ack is enough to detect that the message is supported, no need to deal with the message (which again will be a mess because the message is unreliable and can be sent for many other reasons).

title: Add Functionality to Broadcast to Interface without Explicit Vehicle Connection
author: AlexKlimaj
body:
I am working on recreating the QGC RTK Base station functionality in a C++ application on a raspberry pi. I have the PX4 GPS driver running and now I am trying to figure out how to get mavsdk to broadcast the RTK corrections to all vehicles on two different interfaces. One serial and the other is UDP. 

It does not appear that mavsdk can do a broadcast to all connected vehicles. My approach is to discover all connected vehicles on the serial and UDP connections, then iterate through all of them doing a mavlink passthrough message to send the RTK corrections to each vehicle independently.

answer_comments.body: MAVSDK does not allow to broadcast messages right now. So right now it would just do the same loop as you do :+1:. I am not sure if broadcasting is in the scope of MAVSDK right now, because many things are not expecting to be broadcasted, right? Like all the commands, or basically any targeted message. Or is that incorrect?

I understand that broadcasting some messages may make sense (typically a GNSS base station wants to do just that). But at the MAVSDK level, the user does something like `drone.action.takeoff()`, where `drone` represents a MAVLink system (i.e. a pair of <sysid, compid>). Should MAVSDK allow for broadcasting the `takeoff` command? Because a command is a reliable message, MAVSDK expects to receive an ACK, otherwise it will resend the message. How do you broadcast a reliable message? How many ACKs do you expect, and from which <sysid, compid>? What do you do if one of them times out? Do you consider that your `takeoff` command failed? Or do you tell the user that it "partially succeeded"? Do you give a list of <sysid, compid>, with the result code for each of them?

I don't think it is trivial, but of course we are open to PRs if somebody figures out an nice API doing that in MAVSDK :blush:.
Maybe this is a hint that the MavlinkPassthrough plugin should not be a plugin but a direct API of the Mavsdk class. We could then add some sort of flag to signal the broadcast option.

You can now use the added [RawBytesConnection](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2460e15689052b8cc3ce7fa4052bf584be0e7c83/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L493-L528) and implement whatever sending/receiving protocol you want.

Personally, I'm not a fan of broadcast, so I'm not in favor of including it.

title: Add option to build without curl
author: julianoes
body: For slow compilation (e.g. on embedded boards) it would be nice to be able to build without curl.

answer_comments.body: Sometimes you're in a debugging situation where you just need to rebuild on the device.

Right. But I don't think that adding options in CMakeLists and ifdefs in the code is the right solution for debugging on the device.

If you are debugging curl on the device, then you need to compile it. If you are debugging MAVSDK, then you don't have to recompile curl. Yes, that implies that you may need to not use our superbuild and to learn how to do that (e.g. cross-compile the dependencies separately, copy that on your device and build mavsdk on the device without SUPERBUILD=ON). But that's "basic" dependency management in cmake. I'm happy to write a superbuild to make that easier for most use-cases, but for specific use-cases, I believe that developers should learn how to deal with that.

To me it would be the same as saying "we should make it such that cmake checks if the submodules are correctly synced, because we don't want our developers to have to know about git submodules", and then "cmake should show a warning when people push to their fork without having an 'upstream' branch, because not everyone knows how to work with a fork".

We can do all that, but it results in more code that we need to maintain, and it forces devs to learn about our custom wrappers instead of learning to use the actual tools.

Am I too much of a purist? :laughing:
I agree with your examples but this is more a request that the MAVSDK should be able to build and run with minimal dependencies if required.

For the record: it still requires curl but you can now also use libcurl from the system instead of getting it via git and building it. The way to do so is to use the configure option `cmake -DSUPERBUILD=OFF` for the configure step. Note this is supported as of Ubuntu 18.04 but not 16.04.

title: Serial port connection to PX4 SITL not working with MAVSDK v1.4.4 after upgrading to latest PX4 firmware v1.3.0
author: paulholmstedt
body:
After upgrading one of our Cube Orange PX4 Flight Controllers from PX4 firmware Stable Release v1.12.3 to v1.3.0 MAVSDK v1.4.4 (running on Windows 11 operating system compiled with Visual Studio 2022) is not able to establish a serial connection (i.e. serial://COM16:57600) with the autopilot. It does work when using UDP connection. There is a workaround for it which is to first start QGroundControl and close it down, then connect to the same serial port via MAVSDK. As soon as the autopilot is restarted MAVSDK fails to connect again via serial port until QGroundControl has been run once on the same serial port. The issue has been tested on 2 different flight controllers running SITL. Both tested with my own MAVSDK based software as well with the "fly_mission.cpp" example under MAVSDK GitHub.
![MAVSDK_fail_to_connect_to_serial_port](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/69586779/185954905-77dec52c-e91e-4dc9-a692-7844f5e3da47.jpg)
.
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
> I can't make the config changes describes by @julianoes as they break a few other scripts I'm running

How does it break it? You can change the reset of the config, as long as you do `set_always_send_heartbeat(true)`.

Because it allows to have the NuttShell as well as MAVLink on USB. If you hit enter, you get `nsh`, if you send MAVLink, you get MAVLink. It's kinda neat but broke existing implementations such as MAVSDK.

mavlink协议 是通过 ID 进行区分
一个无人机，在系统中是一个 system，通过system id进行区分
同一个无人的多个功能模块例如照相、gps，通过component id进行区分，不管有多少个connection，都将给更新同一个system。
这些id都在无人机固件中配置的

Translation:
The MAVLink protocol distinguishes a single drone by ID. In the system, a drone is considered one "system," identified by a system ID. Multiple functional modules within the same drone — such as the camera and GPS — are distinguished by component ID. Regardless of how many connections there are, they all update the same system. These IDs are all configured in the drone's firmware.

title: Migration to MAVLink organisation
author: JonasVautherin
body:
Copying @hamishwillee's message on the PX4 Slack, to keep a record of the discussion.

The MAVLink dev team accepted the "MAVLink RFC Proposal" so we'll be taking the Dronecode SDK into the MAVLink organisation and renaming it to the "MAVSDK": https://github.com/mavlink/rfcs/blob/master/text/0011-mavlink-sdk.md

### Code


* [x] Agree on new names for SDK repos
 => Will be `MAVSDK`, `MAVSDK-Proto`, `MAVSDK-Swift`, `MAVSDK-Python`, etc.
* [x] Move all SDK repos into github mavlink org
* [x] Agree new names for namespaces and other code items
 => The documentation and official name is `MAVSDK`, but the code doesn't have to follow that. We will generally prefer lowercase (i.e. namespace: `mavsdk::`), and we may capitalize if necessary (e.g. `class MavSdk`).
* [x] Update code in line with new names
* [ ] Update READMEs with appropriate new links to repos and docs
* [x] Make an official first release. Would this be 1.0?
 => The release will not be 1.0, but just the continuation of current releases, each repo going at its own speed. The Python SDK will be released as `0.1.0` on pip ASAP.
* [x] Make sure all old repositories redirect correctly

### Docs


* [x] Design of new logo & tagline
 => Taken care of in #750.
* [x] Confirm name of docs repo in mavlink org [I think `sdk_docs` to `mavsdk_docs`]
* [x] Move docs repo into mavlink org
* [x] Update head revision docs API reference
* [x] Update docs guide materials
* [ ] Review/update docs on marketing/positioning. Ie where it is hosted and the goals.
* [x] Decide what to do about previous releases/docs. These all will refer to the Dronecode SDK.
* [x] Propose that we delete all the old ones and start from scratch with a master release and initial release
* [x] Re-sync via gitbook
* [x] Get new domain/URL. 
 Current: `https://sdk.dronecode.org/en/`. Proposed: `https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/en/`. This is probably easier than try to do `mavlink.io/mavlink`, `mavlink.io/mavsdk` etc.
* [x] Themes updates
 The theme for the SDK becomes more like the mavlink.io one: https://mavlink.io/en/
* [x] Other dronecode sites will need to have theme updated to point to SDK and any notes about SDK updated too.
* [x] Make sure all old docs links redirect correctly

### Dronecode Website


* [ ] Update top bar
 This is likely to be SLOW process.
* [x] Update SDK page and other mentions.

### Channels


* [x] Discussion board category rename
  * [x] Docs updated (develop, master, 0.16)
  * [x] Update category post link to URL when SDK URL moves: https://discuss.px4.io/t/about-the-mavsdk-category/4234
* [x] Slack channel rename to `#mavsdk`
  * [x] Docs updated (develop, master, 0.16)

title: TCP connection from MAVSDK breaks app after 16 minutes of idle time due to reconnection
author: fibonacci-matrix
body:
I'm developing an app that uses MAVSDK to connect to a device via the built-in MAVSDK TCP connection. MAVSDK has an excellent TCP reconnection mechanism that fits my requirements well, namely the possibility of temporary disconnection. In this case timer is started, which checks every second whether the connection has been restored. But after 16 minutes, this mechanism breaks my app with the message **"socket errorToo many open files"**. 

I did some basic research and the problem is that the MAVSDK in a loop reopens the sockets, but does not close them with the `close` function in case of unsuccessful execution of the `connect` function. 

```
// from tcp_connection.cpp

_socket_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
```

I have tested basic fix on Linux, but I don't know if it will work on other operating systems

comments.body: Would you like to open a PR with your proposed fix? :blush:
Good catch. Yes a PR would be great.
I can do a PR in a few days, but I don't mind if someone else does it. Besides, https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2342 will conflict with my changes
#2342 is merged.

> Maybe I misunderstood the question in the beginning confused. Doesn't [goto_location](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/src/plugins/action/include/plugins/action/action.h#L154) do what you want already?

You are right! I overlooked and didn't notice this exist.

I read all the Examples and thinking maybe there are some functions in follow_me or off_board could achieve my goal, and ignore the Action class. Maybe we can add this goto_location into takeoff_land example, so other people won't miss this?

> Maybe we can add this goto_location into takeoff_land example, so other people won't miss this?

Sure! Good idea! :blush:

I would just like to add a +1 requesting this feature. Especially for UTM applications, which are taking positions in WGS84 coordinates, it'll be very useful to set the own vehicles's position using the same reference frame. Incoming coordinates are not only other vehicle's positions (see [UTM_GLOBAL_POSITION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#UTM_GLOBAL_POSITION)), but might also be temporary and stationary geofences (for obstacles, but also dynamically closed sections of the airspace).

Using the follow-me mode or goto location might be a short-term workaround, but not a good solution, because follow-me is intended for something else (and might interfere with the mobile QGC app setting the target position) and goto has no connection loss failsafe like offboard control. Also the pilot should always have the opportunity to disable control of the companion, which would not be possible using goto. (If I understood the message's documentation correctly, receiving the message once will switch to hold mode with a custom position. Such a mode change might not always be a reasonable choice.)
Hi, I added it in this [PR](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1620)

Alternatively, you can use action.[goto_location](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_action.html#classmavsdk_1_1_action_1afb3546fa994357e491816f2032716818)() which is mostly similar

title: Enable serial and TCP connections for backend
author: julianoes
body:
The backend currently only supports UDP and the port is hardcoded for the backend_bin.

We should use `add_any_connection`, so that we can pass any connection URI.

answer_comments.body: @shrit: Would you have examples illustrating what you mean (instead of the connection URI)?
We already support shortening where applicable, e.g. `udp://` will use the default port on localhost.

I would argue that's too rare of a use case. I would then just have the cli be a list, e.g.: `foo udp://:14540 udp://:14541` and then loop through it.

And note that you can have several vehicles connecting on the same UDP port at the same time, so you don't need a port per vehicle.

linked_prs.title: Enable backend to accept connection URL

linked_issues.title: Arming not working HITL in Python example

comments.body:
Hello,

I was wondering today about the same issue on larger scale (Not exactly for Serial), Maybe we can improve the parser, to accept string and numbers instead of a connection URI.
For instance defining the connection type, UDP, TCP, or Serial and the ip address and the port number differently. This is easier for the user to specify some numbers instead of the entire URI. The less we type, the less error user can have
What do you think?
@shrit: Would you have examples illustrating what you mean (instead of the connection URI)?
We already support shortening where applicable, e.g. `udp://` will use the default port on localhost.

well, actually after creating an instance of 
DronecodeSDK dc_;
we call the function 
dc_.add_any_connection(string);
the string variable contain the entire URI. For example, in the example of documentation we have:
udp://:14540
in the case twe are on udp on localhost  with the port 14540.

A rare use case, If we need to control several vehicles, several instance of controller should be created and we need to specify for each on the port and the connection type.
For this reason, I thought of simplifying even more for the users, like a user could type -P 14540 14550 14560, that is going to take a vector of port number for a set of vehicles.

I would argue that's too rare of a use case. I would then just have the cli be a list, e.g.: `foo udp://:14540 udp://:14541` and then loop through it.

And note that you can have several vehicles connecting on the same UDP port at the same time, so you don't need a port per vehicle.

title: Where can I access camera_action on the Pixhawk 6C?
author: ryanpinney
body: I am using mavsdk python to make missionItems, and at each point on the mission there is an option for camera_action. I will be using camera action(TAKE_PHOTO) and camera action(NONE). What pins can I connect to on the Pixhawk 6C to get these camera triggers? There is no option "actuator" setup in qgroundcontrol for me I am assuming it is because of the airframe type, so I do not know how to configure the pins.

answer_comments.body: I think that this is more a question for PX4. The autopilot is the one "executing" the mission and actually triggering the camera in that case :+1:.

It's a bit confusing because there is the MAVSDK Action TAKE_PHOTO which sends the command [MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE) in PX4 to a potential camera.

However, this doesn't actually set up triggering on PX4. To use triggering, you have to set up the trigger pin in the Actuator setting, and then use MissionRaw and use the command [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST), or [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL)
I don't know. This seems to come up again and again and I just don't seem to get a straight answer.
Awesome, thanks for documenting this. So we can close this? I assume it will get a bit more straightforward once v1.14 is out and the actuator config in QGC shows up by default.

@JonasVautherin @julianoes This is probably a PX4 question too, but there is no "Actuators" menu in my QGC, is that because I selected the wrong or an incompatible airframe?
I don't know. This seems to come up again and again and I just don't seem to get a straight answer.

> @JonasVautherin @julianoes This is probably a PX4 question too, but there is no "Actuators" menu in my QGC, is that because I selected the wrong or an incompatible airframe?

I could solve this just going to the airframe file in /init.d/airframes, disable the mixer and enabling the SYS_CTRL_ALLOC, and then setting all the necessary PWM functions up. In my case, i set `param set-default PWM_AUX_FUNC5 2000  # Camera trigger` for the pwm trigger.

After this i could see the Actuators menu in QGC.

Then, to trigger, make sure you set up the parameters for TRIG_PWM_NEUTRAL and TRIG_PWM_SHOOT. also you could set the TRIG_INTERFACE to generic pwm and TRIG_MODE to 1 for example.

To activate the trigger just send a pymavlink command long [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST) and wait for ACK
Awesome, thanks for documenting this. So we can close this? I assume it will get a bit more straightforward once v1.14 is out and the actuator config in QGC shows up by default.

answer_comments.body: @mrpollo that's nice to auto-generate it but I actually wrote the changelogs manually in the release notes, check out https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/releases. This way it's easier to read and less verbose.

@julianoes The docs release happen after the fact, but should match your releases: https://github.com/dronecore/sdk_docs/releases
At the top of those notes is a link to associated docs. It might be worth creating just that link to the online version of the docs in the software release notes (?)

> Can we please not categorize 'Fixed', 'Closed', 'Merged'.

There is a difference between those sections, but I believe the keywords are more: 'enhancements', 'bugs', 'issues', 'pull requests'. I guess the first two come from the labels. For the last two, the thing is that some PRs are not related to an issue.

If you want to simplify that, maybe we could just have 'bugs' and 'enhancements' (e.g. everything that is not labeled as a bug is an enhancement). And one question is whether we need to list both issues and PRs, or if we can keep only the PRs (because most of the time, issues are closed by PRs, but some PRs are not related to an issue). But then it means that we should make sure we put the 'bug' label on the PRs themselves.

@mrpollo I like the generated report! That is neat for the "full changes" report. And at the top we should probably highlight a few features/write a high-level description of the changes.

Gradle does it this way: they have some kind of blog post that says "now with gradle X.Y, you can do this, this, this and that!", then they have detailed explanations for those "key" features (sometimes linking to actual examples), and I believe they have a link to the full changelog somewhere.

title: Inconsistent documentation in Action class.
author: jwidauer
body:
In the `Action` class the function `goto_location()`s documentation specifies:  
`Send command to reposition the vehicle to a specific WGS84 global position.`

But then underneath it it states:  
`float altitude_amsl_m - Altitude AMSL in meters`

Does this mean the `altitude_amsl_m` will be converted to WGS84 internally or is this a mistake in the documentation?

answer_comments.body:
Good point, thanks for raising this.

I think this is the same that @mzahana found in Dronecode/DronecodeSDK#485 and lead me to create this issue:
https://github.com/PX4/Firmware/issues/10246

Given that, we should make sure that's documented correctly (for now) here.

~I guess the global position would refer to latitude/longitude but is excluding the  altitude.~

I'm confused, I need to check what's exactly going on and then document it.

Almost certainly it is WGS84 position, and AMSL altitude, because that is the underlying definition of the MAVLink frames: https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_FRAME

This is complicated further by the fact that the actual frame might not quite match even that, depending on the positioning hardware (anecdotally, came up in a MAVLink call).

title: Make system-wide install default
author: julianoes
body:
As by @hamishwillee's suggestions in #70:

1. Make system install the default
   - If someone does this build on windows fail and display a message "System install not supported on windows - do `THE COMMAND to build locally`
2. Make docs build against system install path (doxygen config file change). On Windows fail the docs call with a message that"Automated docs builds not supported on Windows".
3. Example code has to stay the same - that should build on windows too.
4. Docs change to separate out how you can point to local installs as a separate topic.
resolution_evidence: maintainer points at the fix: 'done in #73'

answer_comments.body: As far as I read up on it for Windows you add dependencies locally. The global install location would be C:\Windows\system32 but we all remember the dll hell that produced and it doesn't seem to be recommended anymore.
So where do people install shared binaries? More specifically, what will we do if we supply a binary release of DroneCore for Windows?
It gets included in the exe or if linked dynamically supplied in the folder with the exe, I think.

@Stifael Re https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/73#issuecomment-380083682

The documentation is correct and up to date according to our process. The master reflects the current released version (0.1) which is VERY old. The develop reflects the head revision. When we make a release the master in both source code and docs will be updated to the current release version.

The problem here is that we haven't made a release forever, and it is easy to read the master docs alongside the develop code. 

Upshot, if you use the develop docs and develop branch the docs definitely work. The master docs and master branch _should_ work too - but I have not made too much effort to backport docs because a new release has been imminent for ... ever.
